AF.design: Three vertical bands of black, red, and green with the white national emblem centered on the red band.
AF.meaning: Black recalls past struggles, red the blood shed for independence, and green hope and Islam. The white emblem is a mosque with a pulpit and flags, ringed by wheat and the Shahada.

colors.name: Black
colors.meaning: The country’s hard past and earlier flags

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: Sacrifice and the fight for independence

colors.name: White
colors.meaning: Peace, and the color of the mosque emblem

AF.emblem: A mosque with minarets and a mihrab, wheat sheaves, and the Islamic creed.
AF.coatOfArms: The emblem on the flag is the national coat of arms, drawn in white so it stays readable on the red band.

AX.design: A red Nordic cross with a yellow fimbriation on a blue field, in the Scandinavian cross style.
AX.meaning: Blue and yellow come from Sweden, whose language and culture dominate the islands. The red cross nods to Finland, the sovereign country they belong to.

colors.name: Blue
colors.meaning: Swedish heritage, shared with Sweden’s flag

colors.name: Yellow
colors.meaning: Swedish colors and the islands’ historic ties

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: Finland, the country of which Åland is an autonomous part

AX.emblem: A Nordic cross offset toward the hoist, the same family of flags as Denmark, Sweden, and Finland.

AL.design: A red field charged with a black double-headed eagle.
AL.meaning: The double-headed eagle is the emblem of Skanderbeg, the 15th-century hero who resisted Ottoman rule. Red stands for bravery and the blood of those who fought for the nation.

colors.name: Black
colors.meaning: The double-headed eagle of Albanian identity

AL.emblem: A black two-headed eagle, taken from Skanderbeg’s banner and still the national symbol.
AL.coatOfArms: The state coat of arms adds Skanderbeg’s helmet above the same eagle; the everyday flag keeps the eagle alone on red.

DZ.design: A vertical bicolor of green and white with a red star and crescent in the center.
DZ.meaning: Green and the crescent-star pair speak to Islam. White stands for purity, and red for the lives lost in the war of independence from France.
DZ.emblem: A red star and crescent, classic symbols of Islam in North African flags.

AS.design: A blue field with a white triangle at the fly pointing inward, edged in red, and the American eagle holding a staff and a war club.
AS.meaning: The U.S. national colors honor American Samoa’s status as a U.S. territory. The bald eagle carries a Samoan fue (staff of authority) and a uatogi (war club), blending American and Samoan symbols of power.

colors.name: Blue
colors.meaning: The ocean and loyalty, shared with the U.S. flag

colors.name: White
colors.meaning: Purity, from the U.S. color set

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: Courage, again from the U.S. palette

AS.emblem: A bald eagle facing the hoist, holding Samoan chiefly symbols instead of arrows and an olive branch.
AS.coatOfArms: The territorial seal is a different design; the flag uses the U.S. eagle as a living coat-of-arms stand-in.

AD.design: A vertical tricolor of blue, yellow, and red with the coat of arms centered on the yellow band.
AD.meaning: Blue and red come from France; yellow and red from Spain — the two neighbors who jointly protect Andorra. The motto Virtus Unita Fortior means “United virtue is stronger.”

colors.name: Blue
colors.meaning: France, one of Andorra’s two co-princes

colors.name: Yellow
colors.meaning: Spain, and the band that holds the arms

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: Shared by both France and Spain

AD.emblem: The full coat of arms sits on the center stripe.
AD.coatOfArms: A quartered shield: the bishop of Urgell’s miter and staff, the Catalan stripes, the three red bars of Foix, and two cows of Béarn — a map of Andorra’s medieval protectors.

AO.design: Two horizontal bands of red and black with a yellow half-gear, machete, and star in the center.
AO.meaning: Red is the blood of independence; black the African continent. The gear and machete stand for industry and farming, and the star for progress and internationalism — a design born at independence from Portugal.
AO.emblem: A half-cogwheel crossed by a machete, with a star — tools of workers and farmers rather than a traditional coat of arms.

AI.design: A British Blue Ensign with Anguilla’s badge in the fly: three orange dolphins leaping in a circle on white, above a turquoise base.
AI.meaning: The Union Jack marks the island as a British overseas territory. The three dolphins stand for endurance, unity, and strength, and their circle suggests continuity.

colors.name: Blue
colors.meaning: The sea, on a British Blue Ensign

colors.name: White
colors.meaning: Peace and the dolphin badge’s field

colors.name: Orange
colors.meaning: The three dolphins — endurance and friendship

colors.name: Turquoise
colors.meaning: The Caribbean Sea around the island

AI.emblem: Three orange dolphins in a circle, the island’s own badge rather than a full heraldic shield.
AI.coatOfArms: Anguilla’s coat of arms is this same dolphin badge; it replaced an earlier design and is what sits in the ensign’s fly.

AQ.design: A white silhouette of the Antarctic continent on a navy field.
AQ.meaning: Antarctica has no official national flag. This widely used design treats the ice-white continent as the emblem and the dark blue as the surrounding Southern Ocean — a peaceful, non-national symbol for the treaty continent.

colors.name: White
colors.meaning: Ice and the unclaimed, peaceful continent

AQ.emblem: The outline of Antarctica itself, used in place of a coat of arms.

AG.design: A red field with an inverted triangle of black, blue, and white rising from the base, and a rising gold sun on the black band.
AG.meaning: The V-shaped triangle points to victory. Black is the African heritage of the people, blue hope, and white the beaches. The rising sun is a new era; red is the energy of the people.

colors.name: Gold
colors.meaning: The sun and a new era

AG.emblem: A rising golden sun with stylized rays, sitting in the black band of the “V.”

AR.design: Three horizontal bands of light blue, white, and light blue with the golden Sun of May in the center.
AR.meaning: Sky-blue and white were the colors of the 1810 May Revolution against Spain. The Sun of May — a face in a sunburst — marks the start of independence and appears on both the flag and the coat of arms.

colors.name: Sky blue
colors.meaning: The sky, and the revolutionary cockade of 1810

colors.name: White
colors.meaning: The silver of the Río de la Plata and the revolutionary cockade

AR.emblem: The Sun of May, an Inca-inspired sun with a human face.
AR.coatOfArms: The coat of arms also uses the Sun of May above a rising-sun cap of liberty and clasped hands — the flag keeps only the sun.

AM.design: Three equal horizontal bands of red, blue, and orange.
AM.meaning: Red is the blood shed for the nation and the Armenian Highlands. Blue is the sky and the Armenian people. Orange is courage, work, and the fertile land — a tricolor revived after independence from the Soviet Union.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The highlands and lives given for the nation

colors.name: Blue
colors.meaning: The sky and the Armenian people

colors.name: Orange
colors.meaning: Courage, hard work, and fertile land

AW.design: A light blue field with two narrow yellow stripes near the bottom and a red four-pointed star outlined in white at the upper hoist.
AW.meaning: Blue is the sea and sky around Aruba. The yellow stripes are abundance and the island’s two main industries, tourism and gold/aloes. The red star is the island itself, its four points the four main languages, and white the red star’s outline of honesty.

colors.name: Yellow
colors.meaning: Wealth, sunshine, and the island’s key industries

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The island, and love for the homeland

AW.emblem: A four-pointed red star for Aruba and its four languages: Papiamento, Spanish, English, and Dutch.

AU.design: A Blue Ensign with the Commonwealth Star under the Union Jack and the Southern Cross in the fly.
AU.meaning: The Union Jack records British heritage. The large seven-pointed Commonwealth Star stands for the six states plus the territories. The Southern Cross is the sky over Australia.

colors.name: Red and white
colors.meaning: The Union Jack in the canton

colors.name: White stars
colors.meaning: The federation and the southern sky

AU.emblem: The Commonwealth Star (seven points) and the five stars of the Southern Cross.
AU.coatOfArms: The national coat of arms — kangaroo, emu, and shield of the states — is not on the flag; the stars do that work instead.

AT.design: Three equal horizontal bands of red, white, and red.
AT.meaning: Legend says Duke Leopold V’s white surcoat was so soaked in blood after a crusade battle that only the belt stayed white — the oldest national tricolor still in use. Red and white are also the colors of Austria’s historic banners.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: Strength and the historic Austrian banner

colors.name: White
colors.meaning: Honesty, and the legendary unstained belt

AT.coatOfArms: The state flag adds the black eagle coat of arms on the white band; the civil flag shown here is the plain tricolor.

AZ.design: Three horizontal bands of blue, red, and green with a white crescent and eight-pointed star in the center.
AZ.meaning: Blue is the Turkic peoples, red progress and modernity, and green Islam. The crescent is a further Islamic emblem; the eight-pointed star is often read as the eight letters of “Azerbaijan” in Arabic script, or eight Turkic peoples.
AZ.emblem: A crescent and an eight-pointed star, the same pair that appears on the national emblem.

BS.design: A black triangle at the hoist and three horizontal bands of aquamarine, gold, and aquamarine.
BS.meaning: Aquamarine is the sea around the islands, gold the sun and sandy beaches, and black the strength and pride of the people. The triangle points toward the future.

colors.name: Gold
colors.meaning: The sun and the islands’ sands

colors.name: Black
colors.meaning: The strength of the Bahamian people

BS.emblem: A hoist-side triangle rather than a coat of arms — a common Caribbean independence design.

BH.design: A red field with a white serrated band at the hoist, the edge cut into five white triangles.
BH.meaning: Red is a traditional color of Gulf Arab flags. White is peace. The five triangles stand for the five pillars of Islam. The zigzag edge is a Bahraini hallmark that sets it apart from plain red-and-white neighbors.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: A historic Kharijite / Gulf Arab color

colors.name: White
colors.meaning: Peace, and the five pillars of Islam

BH.emblem: Five white points along the hoist, read as the five pillars of Islam.

BD.design: A green field with a red disc slightly toward the hoist.
BD.meaning: Green is the lush land of the Bengal delta. The red disc is the sun rising over Bengal and the blood of those who died for independence in 1971. It is offset so it looks centered when the flag flies.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The rising sun and sacrifice in the liberation war

BD.emblem: A plain red sun, with no star or crescent — a secular national emblem.

BB.design: A vertical tricolor of ultramarine, gold, and ultramarine with a black trident head in the center.
BB.meaning: Blue is the sea and sky, gold the sand and sunshine of Barbados. The broken trident — only the head — means the island broke from colonial rule; the full trident once appeared on the old colonial badge as a symbol of Neptune and Britain.

colors.name: Gold
colors.meaning: The sand and the island’s sunshine

colors.name: Black
colors.meaning: The trident head, and the people

BB.emblem: A broken trident head, a deliberate rewrite of the old colonial Neptune badge.
BB.coatOfArms: The coat of arms keeps a full heraldic scene (pelican, sugar cane, bearded fig). The flag distilled that story into the broken trident.

BY.design: Two horizontal bands of red over green with a vertical red-and-white ornamental pattern at the hoist.
BY.meaning: Red and green come from Soviet-era Belarusian flags, recast after 1995. The hoist pattern is a traditional rushnik embroidery motif — a woven towel used in ceremonies — standing for cultural roots.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The historic banner of Belarus and past sacrifice

colors.name: White
colors.meaning: The embroidered hoist pattern, and spiritual purity

BY.emblem: A vertical band of traditional Belarusian weaving instead of a coat of arms.

BE.design: A vertical tricolor of black, yellow, and red.
BE.meaning: The colors come from the medieval Duchy of Brabant’s coat of arms: a gold lion with red claws on a black shield. After the 1830 revolution they were arranged as vertical bands, echoing the French tricolor’s layout.
BE.coatOfArms: The national arms still show that gold lion on black. The flag flattened the shield into three stripes.

BZ.design: A royal-blue field with thin red stripes at the top and bottom and the coat of arms in a white disc at the center.
BZ.meaning: Blue and white were the colors of the independence movement. Red was added at independence to include the opposition party’s color so the flag would represent the whole country. The coat of arms is unusually detailed for a national flag.

colors.name: Blue
colors.meaning: The People’s United Party and the Caribbean Sea

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The United Democratic Party, added for national unity

colors.name: White
colors.meaning: The disc that holds the arms

BZ.emblem: The full national coat of arms, one of the most complex charges on any flag.
BZ.coatOfArms: A mahogany tree, two supporters (a mestizo with an axe and a Creole with a paddle), tools of logging, a ship, and the motto Sub Umbra Floreo — “I flourish in the shade.”

BJ.design: A green vertical band at the hoist and two horizontal bands of yellow and red.
BJ.meaning: These are the Pan-African colors. Green is hope and revival, yellow the country’s wealth, and red courage. The flag was first adopted at independence in 1960, dropped in the Marxist years, and restored in 1990.

BM.design: A British Red Ensign with Bermuda’s coat of arms in the fly: a red lion holding a shield that shows a wrecked ship.
BM.meaning: The Red Ensign (unusual among British territories, which usually use blue) marks Bermuda’s British link. The wreck is the Sea Venture, which ran aground in 1609 and led to Bermuda’s settlement — a shipwreck as origin story.

colors.name: Green
colors.meaning: The grassy shield in the arms

BM.emblem: A lion holding a smaller shield with the wrecked Sea Venture.
BM.coatOfArms: The entire fly badge is the coat of arms: a red lion (England) presenting the wreck that founded the colony.

BT.design: A diagonal bicolor of gold over orange with a white dragon along the divide, holding jewels.
BT.meaning: Gold is the secular king and civic life; orange is Buddhism. The Druk — Thunder Dragon — is Bhutan’s namesake, and the jewels in its claws are the wealth and security of the people.

colors.name: White
colors.meaning: The purity of the dragon’s thoughts and deeds

BT.emblem: The Druk, a white thunder dragon facing away from the hoist, clutching jewels.

BO.design: Three horizontal bands of red, yellow, and green. The state flag places the coat of arms on the yellow band.
BO.meaning: Red is the blood of heroes, yellow the country’s mineral wealth, and green the fertile land and coca leaf. The civil flag is the plain tricolor; official buildings add the arms.
BO.coatOfArms: An oval arms with Mount Potosí, an alpaca, a sheaf of wheat, and a breadfruit tree — the flag often shown in this app is the civil tricolor without that oval.

BA.design: A blue field with a yellow right triangle and a diagonal row of white stars.
BA.meaning: Blue and yellow echo the European Union flag, a nod to the country’s European path after the 1990s war. The triangle stands for the three main peoples — Bosniaks, Croats, and Serbs — and the stars for Europe.

colors.name: Yellow
colors.meaning: The sun, and the three-sided triangle of the country’s peoples

BA.emblem: A row of seven full white stars and two half-stars, suggesting an infinite line.

BW.design: A light-blue field with a black horizontal stripe edged in white across the center.
BW.meaning: Blue is water — the word pula means both rain and the currency — in a dry country where rain is a blessing. Black and white stand for the zebra and for racial cooperation at independence.

colors.name: Blue
colors.meaning: Water, rain, and the life they bring

colors.name: Black
colors.meaning: The Black majority, and the zebra’s stripes

colors.name: White
colors.meaning: The White minority, and racial harmony

BV.design: A red field with a blue Nordic cross outlined in white — the flag of Norway.
BV.meaning: Bouvet Island is an uninhabited Norwegian dependency, so it flies Norway’s flag. The Nordic cross is Christianity; red, white, and blue were chosen to sit among other Scandinavian and European flags.

colors.name: White
colors.meaning: The cross of Christianity, shared with Denmark

colors.name: Blue
colors.meaning: A cross color linking Norway to Sweden and France

BV.emblem: A Nordic cross; the island has no separate territorial badge.

BR.design: A green field with a yellow rhombus and a blue globe of stars spanned by a white banner reading Ordem e Progresso.
BR.meaning: Green and yellow began as the Braganza and Habsburg royal colors; they are now read as the forests and mineral wealth. The blue globe is the night sky over Rio at the birth of the republic, and each star is a state.

colors.name: Green
colors.meaning: Forests, and the former imperial house of Braganza

colors.name: Blue
colors.meaning: The sky, and the globe of the republic

BR.emblem: A starry globe with the Positivist motto “Order and Progress.” The stars match the constellations over Rio on 15 November 1889.
BR.coatOfArms: The coat of arms is a different design (a star, coffee and tobacco, and a sword). The flag uses the sky-globe instead.

IO.design: A British Blue Ensign with the territory’s badge: a crown, palm, and St. Edward’s Crown over wavy blue-and-white water, with the letters BIOT.
IO.meaning: The Union Jack marks a British territory. The palm and crown stand for the Indian Ocean islands; the wavy lines are the ocean itself.

colors.name: Blue
colors.meaning: The Indian Ocean, on a Blue Ensign

colors.name: White and red
colors.meaning: The Union Jack in the canton

IO.emblem: A crowned palm tree above water, with the initials BIOT.
IO.coatOfArms: The fly badge is the territory’s coat of arms, used because there is no civilian population flag of its own.

VG.design: A British Blue Ensign with a green shield showing Saint Ursula and 11 lamps.
VG.meaning: Columbus named the islands after Saint Ursula and her legendary 11,000 virgins. The badge shows Ursula with 11 lamps — one for each of the main islands — and the motto Vigilate (“Be watchful”).

colors.name: Blue
colors.meaning: A British Blue Ensign for an overseas territory

VG.emblem: Saint Ursula holding a lamp, with more lamps around her.
VG.coatOfArms: The entire fly badge is the coat of arms; the flag is the arms placed on a Blue Ensign, the usual British-territory pattern.

BN.design: A yellow field crossed by black and white diagonal stripes, with the red national crest slightly toward the hoist.
BN.meaning: Yellow is the sultan, the color of royalty in Southeast Asia. White and black are the kingdom’s two chief viziers. The crest holds a parasol, flag wings, and the Arabic motto “Always in service with God’s guidance.”
BN.emblem: The national crest: a mast, royal parasol, upturned wings, and hands on either side.
BN.coatOfArms: The crest on the flag is the coat of arms, drawn in red so it reads clearly on yellow.

BG.design: Three equal horizontal bands of white, green, and red.
BG.meaning: White is peace and dignity, green the land’s fertility, and red the courage of the people. The same tricolor dates to the 19th-century national revival; the communist emblem that once sat in the corner was removed in 1990.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The blood of those who fought for the nation

BG.coatOfArms: The lion coat of arms is used on the presidential standard, not on the national flag.

BF.design: Two horizontal bands of red and green with a yellow five-pointed star in the center.
BF.meaning: Pan-African colors. Red is the revolution that renamed Upper Volta as Burkina Faso (“land of upright people”). Green is abundance; the yellow star is the guiding light of the revolution.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The 1983–84 revolution and the people’s sacrifice

colors.name: Yellow
colors.meaning: Mineral wealth, and the star of guidance

BF.emblem: A single five-pointed star, a common revolutionary emblem in West Africa.

BI.design: A white saltire dividing red and green triangles, with a white disc holding three red six-pointed stars outlined in green.
BI.meaning: Red is independence, green hope, and white peace. The three stars are Unity, Work, Progress — the national motto — and also the three main ethnic groups: Hutu, Tutsi, and Twa.
BI.emblem: Three six-pointed stars for the motto and the country’s three peoples.

KH.design: Three horizontal bands of blue, red (double width), and blue with the white outline of Angkor Wat in the center.
KH.meaning: Blue is royalty and brotherhood, red the nation and courage, and white the religion (Buddhism). Angkor Wat is the kingdom’s great temple and the only building that is the main charge on a national flag.
KH.emblem: Angkor Wat, drawn in white on the wide red band.
KH.coatOfArms: The royal arms are a different, much busier design. The flag uses the temple as a simpler national emblem.

CM.design: A vertical tricolor of green, red, and yellow with a yellow five-pointed star in the red band.
CM.meaning: Pan-African colors. Green is the forests of the south, yellow the savannas of the north and the sun, and red unity. The star is “the star of unity” after the 1961 joining of French and British Cameroons.

colors.name: Yellow
colors.meaning: The northern savanna and the sun

CM.emblem: A single yellow star for national unity.

CA.design: A red-white-red vertical triband (a Canadian pale) with an 11-pointed red maple leaf in the center.
CA.meaning: Red and white were proclaimed Canada’s colors by King George V in 1921. The maple leaf had already been a popular emblem for a century. The current leaf has 11 points for a clean, modern silhouette, not for 11 provinces.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: Sacrifice in wartime, and the British heritage color

colors.name: White
colors.meaning: Purity, and the French royal color paired with red

CA.emblem: A stylized maple leaf — Canada’s best-known symbol, used instead of the royal coat of arms.
CA.coatOfArms: The full arms (lions, fleurs-de-lis, maple leaves) appear on official documents. The 1965 flag replaced the old Canadian Red Ensign that had carried those arms.

CV.design: A blue field with a white-red-white stripe toward the bottom and a ring of ten yellow stars.
CV.meaning: Blue is the Atlantic. The stripe is the road of progress (white for peace, red for effort). Ten stars are the ten islands, arranged in a circle for unity.

colors.name: Yellow
colors.meaning: The sun, and the ten island stars

CV.emblem: A circle of ten stars for the ten islands of Cape Verde.

BQ.design: A white hoist triangle, a yellow fly triangle, a blue band, and a black-edged red six-pointed star — the flag of Bonaire, the largest island of the Caribbean Netherlands.
BQ.meaning: The three islands (Bonaire, Sint Eustatius, Saba) have their own flags; Bonaire’s is the one commonly used for the group. Blue is the sea, yellow the sun, white peace, and the compass-like star Bonaire’s six neighborhoods and its navigation heritage.

colors.name: Yellow
colors.meaning: The sun and the island’s warmth

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The star, and the blood of the people

BQ.emblem: A six-pointed red star used as a compass rose.

KY.design: A British Blue Ensign with a shield of three stars, a lion, and a turtle on a coil of rope.
KY.meaning: The Union Jack marks a British overseas territory. The lion is England; three stars are the three islands (Grand Cayman, Cayman Brac, Little Cayman); the turtle and rope recall seafaring and turtle fishing.

colors.name: Blue
colors.meaning: The sea, on a Blue Ensign

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The English lion in the arms

KY.emblem: A shield with a lion, three stars, a turtle, and rope.
KY.coatOfArms: The fly badge is the coat of arms granted in 1958; the flag is those arms on a Blue Ensign.

CF.design: Four horizontal bands of blue, white, green, and yellow with a vertical red bar through the center and a yellow star at the upper hoist.
CF.meaning: Blue, white, and red nod to France; green, yellow, and red are Pan-African. Together they mean the country stands between Europe and Africa. The star is independence; the red bar is the blood that unites all people.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The blood that binds the nation

CF.emblem: A yellow five-pointed star for independence.

TD.design: A vertical tricolor of blue, yellow, and red.
TD.meaning: Blue is the sky, water, and the south; yellow the sun and the Sahara in the north; red progress and sacrifice. The layout matches Romania’s flag, so Chad’s blue is a deeper indigo to tell them apart.

colors.name: Blue
colors.meaning: Sky, hope, and the southern waters

colors.name: Yellow
colors.meaning: The sun and the desert north

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: Progress and the blood of martyrs

CL.design: A white band over a red band, with a blue canton holding a single white star.
CL.meaning: White is the snow of the Andes, red the blood of independence, and blue the sky. The lone star is honor and a guide toward progress — a design from the independence wars against Spain.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The blood of those who won independence

CL.emblem: A single five-pointed white star, the “Star of Magnanimity.”

CN.design: A red field with one large gold star and four smaller stars in an arc at the upper hoist.
CN.meaning: Red is the communist revolution and the Chinese people. The large star is the Communist Party; the four smaller stars are the social classes united around it, as described when the flag was chosen in 1949.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The revolution and the Chinese nation

colors.name: Gold
colors.meaning: Brightness and the yellow-skinned people in the original explanation

CN.emblem: Five stars: one large, four small, a design by Zeng Liansong.

CX.design: A blue field with the Southern Cross in the fly and a gold disc at the hoist holding the green outline of the island and a golden bosunbird.
CX.meaning: Blue is the Indian Ocean. The Southern Cross places the island in the Australian sky. The gold disc is phosphate, the island’s historic wealth, and the bosunbird is a local seabird.

colors.name: Green
colors.meaning: The island’s outline on the disc

CX.emblem: A golden bosunbird over the map of Christmas Island.

CC.design: A green field with a gold crescent at the hoist and the Southern Cross in the fly, plus a gold disc with a palm tree between them.
CC.meaning: Green and the crescent honor the islands’ Malay Muslim community. The Southern Cross marks Australia. The palm is the cocos (coconut) that gave the islands their name.

colors.name: Green
colors.meaning: The islands’ vegetation and Islamic heritage

colors.name: Gold
colors.meaning: The sun, the crescent, and the palm

CC.emblem: A crescent, a palm tree, and the Southern Cross together on one flag.

CO.design: Three horizontal bands of yellow (double width), blue, and red.
CO.meaning: Yellow is sovereignty and the land’s gold. Blue is the oceans and rivers that wash Colombia. Red is the blood of independence. The same family of flags is shared with Ecuador and Venezuela, all once Gran Colombia.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The blood of those who won independence

CO.coatOfArms: The state flag adds the coat of arms on the yellow band; the civil flag is the plain tricolor.

KM.design: Four horizontal bands of yellow, white, red, and blue with a green hoist triangle holding a white crescent and four stars.
KM.meaning: The four stripes and four stars are the four islands. Green and the crescent are Islam. Each stripe color is also one island’s traditional color.
KM.emblem: A crescent and four stars for Islam and the four islands.

CG.design: A diagonal tricolor of green, yellow, and red, the yellow band running from lower hoist to upper fly.
CG.meaning: Pan-African colors. Green is the forests, yellow friendship and the land’s wealth, and red the people’s courage. Restored after the one-party years that had used a red flag with a hoe and hammer.

CK.design: A British Blue Ensign with a ring of 15 white stars in the fly.
CK.meaning: The Union Jack records ties to New Zealand and the Crown. Fifteen stars are the 15 islands of the group, arranged in a circle for unity.
CK.emblem: A circle of 15 stars instead of a coat of arms.

CR.design: Five horizontal stripes of blue, white, red (double width), white, and blue. The state flag adds the coat of arms on the red band.
CR.meaning: Blue is the sky, opportunities, and perseverance. White is peace and wisdom. Red is the warmth of the people and the blood of independence. The design was inspired by the French tricolor after Europe’s 1848 revolutions.

colors.name: Blue
colors.meaning: The sky, the sea, and perseverance

CR.coatOfArms: Three volcanoes between two oceans, seven stars for the provinces, and a rising sun — often placed on the red stripe of official flags.

HR.design: A horizontal tricolor of red, white, and blue with the chequy coat of arms in the center.
HR.meaning: Red-white-blue are the pan-Slavic colors. The shield of red and white squares — the šahovnica — is Croatia’s medieval arms and the flag’s unmistakable emblem.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: A pan-Slavic color, and the chequy squares

colors.name: White
colors.meaning: A pan-Slavic color, and the chequy squares

colors.name: Blue
colors.meaning: A pan-Slavic color, and the Adriatic

HR.emblem: The šahovnica shield crowned with five smaller historic shields.
HR.coatOfArms: The flag carries the full modern coat of arms: the chequy plus crests for the oldest Croatian regions.

CU.design: Five blue and white stripes with a red hoist triangle holding a white star.
CU.meaning: The stripes are the original three Cuban departments, later five. The triangle is equality and Freemason ideals of the independence movement. The lone star is independence itself — designed in 1849, decades before it became official.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The blood of independence, and equality

CU.emblem: A single white star, La Estrella Solitaria.

CW.design: A blue field with a yellow stripe below the center and two white stars at the upper hoist.
CW.meaning: Blue is the sea and sky. Yellow is the sun and the cheerful character of the people. The two stars are Curaçao and Klein Curaçao; their five points are the five continents from which the island’s people came.

colors.name: Blue
colors.meaning: The sea and sky around the island

colors.name: Yellow
colors.meaning: The sun and a bright spirit

colors.name: White
colors.meaning: Peace, and the two island stars

CW.emblem: Two five-pointed stars for the two islands and five continents of origin.

CY.design: A white field with a copper-orange silhouette of the island and two green olive branches below.
CY.meaning: White and the olive branches are peace between Greek and Turkish Cypriots. The island is colored copper because Cyprus was famous for copper in antiquity — the metal’s name is related to the island’s.
CY.emblem: The map of Cyprus itself, a rare choice for a national flag.

CZ.design: A white band over a red band with a blue triangle at the hoist.
CZ.meaning: White and red are the historic colors of Bohemia. Blue was added for Moravia and Slovakia when the flag was created for Czechoslovakia; Czechia kept the same flag after the 1993 split.

colors.name: Blue
colors.meaning: Moravia, and the old Czechoslovak union

DK.design: A red field with a white Nordic cross offset toward the hoist.
DK.meaning: Legend says the Dannebrog fell from the sky during a 13th-century battle in Estonia. It is often called the oldest national flag still in use. The cross is Christianity; the off-center hoist became the model for all Nordic flags.
DK.emblem: A Nordic cross — the parent of the Scandinavian flag family.

DJ.design: Two horizontal bands of light blue and green with a white hoist triangle holding a red star.
DJ.meaning: Blue is the Issa people and the sea; green the Afar people and the earth. White is peace; the red star is unity and independence.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: Unity and the star of independence

DJ.emblem: A red five-pointed star for unity.

DM.design: A green field with a cross of yellow, black, and white, and a red disc holding a purple Sisserou parrot.
DM.meaning: Green is the island’s forests. The cross is Christianity and the trinity of colors: yellow for sunshine and bananas, black for the soil and African heritage, white for rivers and purity. The parrot is found only on Dominica.

colors.name: Black
colors.meaning: The rich soil and African heritage

colors.name: Purple
colors.meaning: The Sisserou parrot, a rare flag color

DM.emblem: A Sisserou parrot facing the hoist, ringed by ten green stars for the parishes.
DM.coatOfArms: The coat of arms is a more formal shield with a lion and banana tree. The flag uses the parrot as a living national emblem.

DO.design: A white cross dividing blue and red quarters, with the coat of arms in the center.
DO.meaning: Blue is liberty, red the blood of heroes, and the white cross is salvation. The arms sit in the cross’s center — one of the few flags that always shows the full coat of arms.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The blood of the independence fighters

DO.emblem: The national coat of arms on the crossing of the white cross.
DO.coatOfArms: A shield with a Bible, a cross, and the motto Dios, Patria, Libertad, flanked by palm and laurel — the flag is built around these arms.

CD.design: A sky-blue field with a yellow star at the upper hoist and a red diagonal stripe edged in yellow.
CD.meaning: Blue is peace. The large star is unity. Red is the blood of martyrs, and yellow the country’s mineral wealth. A return to a design close to the 1960s independence flag.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The blood of those who died for the country

CD.emblem: A single large yellow star for unity.

EC.design: Bands of yellow (double width), blue, and red with the coat of arms in the center.
EC.meaning: The same Gran Colombia colors as Colombia and Venezuela. Yellow is the sun and wealth, blue the sky and ocean, red the blood of heroes. Ecuador’s flag is told apart by the arms in the middle.
EC.emblem: The full coat of arms, including Chimborazo and a steamship on the Guayas.
EC.coatOfArms: An oval with Mount Chimborazo, a river steamer, a condor, and the zodiac — the flag’s centerpiece and the sure way to tell Ecuador from Colombia.

EG.design: Three horizontal bands of red, white, and black with the gold Eagle of Saladin in the white band.
EG.meaning: The Arab Liberation flag: red for the struggle, white for a bright future, black for the dark past of oppression. The eagle is a medieval sultan’s emblem reused as a modern republican symbol.
EG.emblem: The Eagle of Saladin holding a scroll with the country’s name.
EG.coatOfArms: The eagle on the flag is the coat of arms, drawn in gold on the white band.

SV.design: Three horizontal bands of blue, white, and blue with the coat of arms in the center.
SV.meaning: Blue is the sky and the two oceans that frame Central America. White is peace. The arms in the middle carry the national motto and five volcanoes for the old Federal Republic of Central America.
SV.emblem: The coat of arms on the white band.
SV.coatOfArms: Five volcanoes, a cap of liberty, and the motto Dios, Unión, Libertad — the civil flag may omit the arms, but the state flag shows them.

GQ.design: Three horizontal bands of green, white, and red with a blue triangle at the hoist and the coat of arms in the center.
GQ.meaning: Green is the forests, white peace, red the fight for independence, and blue the sea that links the mainland to the islands. The silk-cotton tree on the arms is a traditional meeting place.
GQ.coatOfArms: A silk-cotton tree, six stars for the mainland and five islands, and the motto Unidad, Paz, Justicia.

ER.design: A red isosceles triangle from the hoist, with green and blue triangles, and a yellow olive wreath on the red.
ER.meaning: Green is farming, blue the Red Sea, and red the blood of the 30-year independence war. The wreath and upright olive branch come from the liberation front’s emblem.

colors.name: Yellow
colors.meaning: The olive wreath of peace and mineral wealth

ER.emblem: An olive branch in a wreath, adopted from the EPLF flag.

EE.design: Three equal horizontal bands of blue, black, and white.
EE.meaning: Blue is the sky, sea, and loyalty. Black is the soil and a dark past. White is snow, birch bark, and the bright future. First blessed in 1884 as a student society flag, then the national flag.

SZ.design: Horizontal bands of blue, yellow, red (wide), yellow, and blue, with a black-and-white Nguni shield and two spears on the red band.
SZ.meaning: Blue is peace, yellow the mineral resources, and red the battles of the past. The shield and spears are protection; the black-and-white hide stands for people of different backgrounds living together.
SZ.emblem: A Nguni shield with a staff and two spears, the same idea as the royal coat of arms.

ET.design: Three horizontal bands of green, yellow, and red with a blue disc holding a yellow pentagram and rays.
ET.meaning: Green, yellow, and red are the original Pan-African colors, taken from Ethiopia itself. Green is the land, yellow peace and hope, red strength. The star is the diversity of the nations, nationalities, and peoples, shining equally.
ET.emblem: A five-pointed star with rays, the emblem of the federal republic.

FK.design: A British Blue Ensign with the islands’ coat of arms: a ram, a ship, and the motto Desire the Right.
FK.meaning: The Union Jack marks a British overseas territory. The ram is sheep farming; the ship is Desire, the vessel that sighted the islands in 1592.

colors.name: Blue
colors.meaning: The South Atlantic, on a Blue Ensign

FK.coatOfArms: A shield with a ram above the ship Desire — the entire fly badge of the flag.

FO.design: A white field with a red Nordic cross fimbriated in blue.
FO.meaning: White is the spray of the sea and the sky. Red and blue come from traditional Faroese clothing and also nod to Norway and Denmark. Offset like other Nordic crosses.

colors.name: White
colors.meaning: The sky and the foam of the waves

FO.emblem: A Nordic cross in the Faroese color order.

FJ.design: A light-blue British ensign with Fiji’s shield in the fly: a British lion, sugar cane, a coconut palm, bananas, and a dove of peace.
FJ.meaning: Light blue is the Pacific. The Union Jack records the British past. The shield keeps colonial-era crops and a dove, a mix still used after independence.
FJ.coatOfArms: The fly badge is the shield from the coat of arms, without the supporters (Fijian warriors) that appear on the full arms.

FI.design: A white field with a blue Nordic cross.
FI.meaning: Blue is the lakes and the sky; white is the snow of winter. A Nordic cross places Finland in the Scandinavian flag family even though Finnish is not a Scandinavian language.
FI.emblem: A Nordic cross. The state flag adds the lion coat of arms at the crossing.

FR.design: A vertical tricolor of blue, white, and red.
FR.meaning: Blue and red are Paris; white was the old royal color. Combined in the Revolution, they became liberty, equality, and fraternity in later readings. The tricolor inspired dozens of other national flags.

colors.name: White
colors.meaning: The historic royal color, and later equality

FR.coatOfArms: France has no official coat of arms on the flag. The tricolor replaced the old royal fleurs-de-lis banner.

GF.design: A diagonal bicolor of green and yellow with a red five-pointed star in the center — a widely used local flag. Officially the French tricolor also flies.
GF.meaning: Green is the Amazon forest, yellow gold and the sun. The red star is socialism and the workers’ movement that popularized the design. French Guiana is an overseas department of France.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The star of the workers’ movement

GF.emblem: A single red star on the diagonal divide.

PF.design: Two red bands around a wide white band holding a disc with a Polynesian canoe and a golden sun.
PF.meaning: Red and white come from historical Tahitian flags. The canoe with five figures is the five island groups; the sun and waves are life in the Pacific.

colors.name: Gold
colors.meaning: The sun on the emblem disc

PF.emblem: A double-hulled canoe under a radiating sun, the territorial coat of arms.

TF.design: A blue field with the French tricolor in the canton and five white stars plus the letters TAAF in the fly.
TF.meaning: Blue is the Southern Ocean. The tricolor marks French sovereignty. Five stars are the districts of the territory; TAAF is the French abbreviation.

colors.name: White
colors.meaning: The stars of the five districts

TF.emblem: Five stars and the letters TAAF instead of a pictorial coat of arms.

GA.design: Three equal horizontal bands of green, yellow, and blue.
GA.meaning: Green is the equatorial forests. Yellow is the sun and the equator, which crosses the country. Blue is the Atlantic.

GM.design: Three horizontal bands of red, blue, and green, the blue edged in white.
GM.meaning: Red is the sun and the savanna. Blue is the Gambia River, the country’s spine. Green is the land and forests. White is peace and unity.

GE.design: A white field with a large red St. George’s cross and four smaller red crosses in the quarters.
GE.meaning: White is innocence and purity. The five red crosses are a medieval Georgian Christian banner, revived after independence as a clear break from the Soviet-era flag.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The five holy crosses, and courage

GE.emblem: Five St. George-style crosses, the Jerusalem-cross layout used as a national Christian emblem.

DE.design: Three equal horizontal bands of black, red, and gold.
DE.meaning: The colors come from 19th-century liberal and unification movements, later tied to the 1848 revolutions. Black-red-gold is the democratic Germany; black-white-red was the old empire. Gold is often called yellow in everyday speech but the official name is gold.

colors.name: Black
colors.meaning: Determination, and the liberal student banners

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The blood of those who fought for freedom

colors.name: Gold
colors.meaning: The light of a free future

DE.coatOfArms: The federal eagle appears on the state flag used by government, not on the everyday civil tricolor.

GH.design: Three horizontal bands of red, yellow, and green with a black five-pointed star in the center.
GH.meaning: The first African flag to use these colors as a statement of independence, later copied across the continent. Red is the blood of the struggle, yellow mineral wealth, green the forests, and the black star African freedom.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The blood of those who won independence

GH.emblem: The Black Star, taken from Marcus Garvey’s Black Star Line.

GI.design: Two horizontal bands of white and red with a red triple-towered castle and a gold key hanging from its gate.
GI.meaning: The castle is the fortress of Gibraltar. The key is the motto “Key to the Mediterranean” — the Rock guards the strait. The design comes from the coat of arms granted by Spain’s Queen Isabella in 1502, kept after the British takeover.

colors.name: White
colors.meaning: The upper field of the historic arms

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The lower field, and the castle

GI.emblem: A red castle and a hanging gold key.
GI.coatOfArms: The flag is the coat of arms turned into a banner — castle and key, unchanged for five centuries.

GR.design: Nine blue and white stripes with a white cross in a blue canton.
GR.meaning: Blue is the sea and sky; white is the foam of the waves and the purity of the independence struggle. The cross is Eastern Orthodoxy. Nine stripes are often read as the syllables of Eleftheria i Thanatos — “Freedom or Death.”

colors.name: White
colors.meaning: Waves, and the struggle for freedom

GR.emblem: A Christian cross in the canton.

GL.design: Two horizontal bands of white and red with a slightly off-center disc that swaps those colors.
GL.meaning: White is the ice cap; red is the ocean. The disc is the sun sinking into or rising from the sea — a Nordic-style flag without a cross, designed by Thue Christiansen.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The sea, and a nod to Denmark’s Dannebrog

GL.emblem: A sun disc that is half white, half red.

GD.design: A red border with six gold stars, a diagonal yellow and green field, a central red disc with a star, and a nutmeg at the hoist.
GD.meaning: Red is courage, yellow the sun and warmth of the people, green the vegetation. Seven stars are the seven parishes. The nutmeg marks the “Isle of Spice.”

colors.name: Yellow
colors.meaning: The sun and the people’s warmth

GD.emblem: A nutmeg and seven gold stars for the parishes.

GP.design: A black-red-yellow field with a green sugar cane and sun, used locally; the official flag is the French tricolor.
GP.meaning: Guadeloupe is a French overseas department, so the tricolor is official. Local flags often show a sun and sugar cane on black, red, and gold — colors of the Caribbean and of the island’s plantation past.

colors.name: Black, red, and gold
colors.meaning: Popular local colors for the sun, soil, and people

GP.emblem: A radiant sun and sugar cane on many unofficial local flags.

GU.design: A blue field with a red border and a pointed oval seal: a proa, a coconut tree, and the name Guam.
GU.meaning: Blue is the Pacific. Red is the blood of those who died in war. The proa is traditional seafaring; the coconut tree is livelihood; the pointed shape recalls a sling stone, an ancient Chamorro weapon.
GU.emblem: The territorial seal in a sling-stone shape.
GU.coatOfArms: The seal on the flag is Guam’s coat of arms: proa, coconut, and the cliff of Two Lovers Point.

GT.design: Three vertical bands of light blue, white, and light blue with the coat of arms on the white band.
GT.meaning: Blue is the two oceans that border Central America. White is peace. The quetzal on the arms is liberty — the bird is said to die in captivity.
GT.coatOfArms: A quetzal perched on a scroll dated 15 September 1821, crossed rifles and swords, and laurel — the flag’s centerpiece.

GG.design: A white field with a red St. George’s cross and a gold Norman cross in the center.
GG.meaning: The red cross is England. The gold cross is William the Conqueror, tying the island to Normandy. A banner of the old gold cross alone is still used as the governor’s flag.
GG.emblem: A gold cross with flared ends at the center of St. George’s cross.

GN.design: A vertical tricolor of red, yellow, and green.
GN.meaning: Pan-African colors in the same layout as France, Guinea’s former colonial power, but with African meaning: red is labor and sacrifice, yellow the sun and wealth, green the vegetation.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: Labor and the blood of the struggle

GW.design: A red vertical band at the hoist with a black star, and two horizontal bands of yellow and green.
GW.meaning: Pan-African colors from the PAIGC independence movement, shared for a time with Cape Verde. The black star is African freedom.
GW.emblem: A black star on the red hoist band.

GY.design: A green field with a gold triangle edged in white and a red triangle edged in black, both from the hoist — the “Golden Arrowhead.”
GY.meaning: Green is the forests, gold mineral wealth, white the rivers, red zeal, and black endurance. Designed with help from vexillologist Whitney Smith at independence.
GY.emblem: The arrowhead triangles themselves, pointing toward the future.

HT.design: Two horizontal bands of blue and red with the coat of arms on a white square in the center.
HT.meaning: Blue and red come from tearing the white out of the French tricolor during the revolution — a rejection of the colonizer. The arms show weapons under a palm and the motto L’Union fait la force.

colors.name: Blue
colors.meaning: The sky, and one half of the revolutionary bicolor

colors.name: White
colors.meaning: The square that holds the arms

HT.coatOfArms: A palm tree topped with a cap of liberty, cannons, flags, and the motto “Unity makes strength” — always shown on the state flag.

HM.design: The flag of Australia: a Blue Ensign with the Commonwealth Star and Southern Cross.
HM.meaning: Heard Island and McDonald Islands are an uninhabited Australian territory, so they fly the Australian national flag. There is no separate territorial ensign.

colors.name: White stars
colors.meaning: The Southern Cross over the Southern Ocean

HN.design: Three horizontal bands of turquoise, white, and turquoise with five turquoise stars in the center.
HN.meaning: The Central American blue-white-blue, now specified as turquoise. Five stars are the five nations of the old Federal Republic. The 2022 law set the exact shade after years of navy vs. turquoise debate.

colors.name: Turquoise
colors.meaning: The sky, the two seas, and brotherhood

HN.emblem: Five stars for the five Central American republics.

HK.design: A red field with a white five-petaled Bauhinia flower, each petal holding a red star.
HK.meaning: Red ties Hong Kong to China. The Bauhinia is a local flower. Five stars echo China’s flag and the idea of the Chinese people; the white flower is “one country, two systems.”

colors.name: White
colors.meaning: The Bauhinia, and a distinct local system

HK.emblem: A stylized Bauhinia blakeana with a star on each petal.
HK.coatOfArms: The regional emblem is this same flower in a red disc; the colonial coat of arms was retired in 1997.

HU.design: Three equal horizontal bands of red, white, and green.
HU.meaning: Red is strength, white fidelity, and green hope — a reading from the 19th century. The tricolor dates to the 1848 revolution. Communist emblems that once sat in the center were torn out in 1956 and never put back.
HU.coatOfArms: The striped shield with the patriarchal cross is used on the state flag, not on the plain civil tricolor.

IS.design: A blue field with a red Nordic cross outlined in white.
IS.meaning: Blue is the mountains and the Atlantic. White is ice and snow. Red is the volcanoes and the fire under the ice — a landscape in three colors, in the Nordic-cross family.
IS.emblem: A Nordic cross in Iceland’s landscape colors.

IN.design: Three horizontal bands of saffron, white, and green with a navy 24-spoke Ashoka Chakra in the center.
IN.meaning: Saffron is courage and sacrifice, white truth and peace, green faith and fertility. The wheel is the “wheel of law” from the lion capital of Ashoka — duty in motion, replacing the spinning wheel of the independence-movement flag.
IN.emblem: The 24-spoke Dharma Chakra, also found on the national emblem’s lion capital.
IN.coatOfArms: The Lion Capital of Ashoka is the official emblem; the flag uses only its wheel.

ID.design: Two equal horizontal bands of red and white.
ID.meaning: Red is the body and courage; white is the soul and purity — a pairing that appears in 13th-century Majapahit banners. It is a simpler cousin of the Monaco flag, in a different proportion.

IR.design: Three horizontal bands of green, white, and red with a red emblem in the center and stylized Allahu Akbar written along the edges of the white band.
IR.meaning: Green is Islam, white peace, red courage. The central emblem is a stylized word Allah that also suggests a tulip, a martyr’s flower in Iranian culture. The takbir is written 22 times, for the date of the 1979 revolution.
IR.emblem: A red monogram of Allah that doubles as a tulip.
IR.coatOfArms: That same monogram is the national emblem, designed by Hamid Nadimi after the revolution.

IQ.design: Three horizontal bands of red, white, and black with the green takbir Allahu Akbar in Kufic script on the white band.
IQ.meaning: The Arab Liberation colors. The takbir was added under Saddam Hussein and kept, in a new script, after 2008 as a statement that God is greater than any regime. Stars that once sat on the white band were removed.

colors.name: Black
colors.meaning: The dark past, and the Abbasid heritage

IQ.emblem: The words Allahu Akbar in Kufic calligraphy instead of a pictorial coat of arms.

IE.design: A vertical tricolor of green, white, and orange.
IE.meaning: Green is the Gaelic and nationalist tradition. Orange is the Protestant Williamite tradition. White is the lasting peace that should sit between them — a flag of reconciliation first flown in 1848.

IM.design: A red field with the triskelion: three armored legs joined at the thigh, in silver and gold.
IM.meaning: The Three Legs of Man are a medieval emblem of the island, possibly from Sicily. The motto around the full arms is Quocunque Jeceris Stabit — “Whichever way you throw it, it will stand.”
IM.emblem: The triskelion of three running legs.
IM.coatOfArms: The flag is a banner of the arms: the same three legs on red.

IL.design: A white field with two horizontal blue stripes and a blue Star of David in the center.
IL.meaning: The design comes from the tallit, the Jewish prayer shawl. The hexagram is the Magen David, a long-standing Jewish emblem. Blue and white were already Zionist colors in the 19th century.

colors.name: Blue
colors.meaning: The stripes of the tallit, and the heavens

IL.emblem: The Star of David, also called the Shield of David.

IT.design: A vertical tricolor of green, white, and red.
IT.meaning: Inspired by the French tricolor and first used by Napoleonic Italian republics. Green is often read as the plains, white the Alps, and red the blood of the Risorgimento — or hope, faith, and charity.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The blood of unification, and charity

IT.coatOfArms: The republican emblem (a star, cogwheel, and olive and oak) is not placed on the national flag.

CI.design: A vertical tricolor of orange, white, and green — the mirror image of Ireland’s flag.
CI.meaning: Orange is the savanna of the north and the harvest. White is peace and unity. Green is the forests of the south. The same three colors as Ireland, but swapped and with a different story.

colors.name: Orange
colors.meaning: The northern savanna and a fruitful land

JM.design: A gold saltire dividing black and green triangles.
JM.meaning: Black is the strength and creativity of the people. Gold is sunshine and natural wealth. Green is hope and agriculture. Often summed up as “Hardships there are, but the land is green and the sun shineth.”

colors.name: Gold
colors.meaning: The sun and the island’s wealth

JP.design: A white field with a red disc in the center — the Hinomaru, or sun disc.
JP.meaning: Japan is the “land of the rising sun.” The red disc is the sun, tied in myth to the goddess Amaterasu. White is honesty and purity. The design is centuries old; a 1999 law made it the official national flag.
JP.emblem: A plain sun disc, without rays — the civil Hinomaru, not the military rising-sun ensign.

JE.design: A white field with a red saltire and the badge of Jersey in the upper quadrant: a red shield with three gold leopards and a Plantagenet crown.
JE.meaning: The red saltire is St. Patrick, long used on the island. The leopards are England; the crown marks Jersey’s special link to the Crown, not to the UK parliament.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: St. Patrick’s saltire and the English shield

JE.coatOfArms: Three gold leopards on red, the arms of England, topped with a Plantagenet crown — Jersey’s badge on the flag.

JO.design: Black, white, and green horizontal bands with a red hoist triangle holding a white seven-pointed star.
JO.meaning: The Pan-Arab colors of the 1916 Arab Revolt. Black is the Abbasids, white the Umayyads, green the Fatimids, and red the Hashemite dynasty. The seven-pointed star is the seven verses of the Fatiha, the opening of the Qur’an.
JO.emblem: A seven-pointed white star for the seven verses of the Fatiha.

KZ.design: A sky-blue field with a gold sun and soaring eagle, plus a gold ornamental stripe at the hoist.
KZ.meaning: Blue is the endless sky and the Turkic peoples. The sun is wealth and life; its 32 rays are traditional grains. The steppe eagle is freedom. The hoist pattern is a national ornament called koshkar-muiz (ram’s horns).

colors.name: Sky blue
colors.meaning: The sky, peace, and Turkic heritage

colors.name: Gold
colors.meaning: The sun, the eagle, and prosperity

KZ.emblem: A sun with 32 rays and a steppe eagle, plus a vertical folk pattern.

KE.design: Black, red, and green bands edged in white, with a Maasai shield and two spears in the center.
KE.meaning: Black is the people, red the blood of independence, green the land, and white peace. The shield and spears are defense of freedom — a warrior emblem used as a coat of arms.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The blood of the independence struggle

KE.emblem: A red Maasai shield with crossed spears.
KE.coatOfArms: The same shield appears on the national arms, held by lions; the flag uses the shield alone.

KI.design: A red upper half with a gold frigatebird over a rising sun, and a blue-and-white wavy lower half.
KI.meaning: The design is a banner of the coat of arms. The frigatebird is command of the sea; 17 sun rays are the 16 Gilbert Islands plus Banaba. Waves are the Pacific.
KI.coatOfArms: The flag is the coat of arms turned sideways: bird, sun, and ocean.

XK.design: A blue field with a gold silhouette of Kosovo and six white stars in an arc above it.
XK.meaning: Blue and the stars echo the European Union flag. The six stars are the six main communities: Albanians, Serbs, Turks, Gorani, Roma, and Bosniaks. Gold is the map of the country.
XK.emblem: The map of Kosovo under six stars.

KW.design: A black trapezoid at the hoist and three horizontal bands of green, white, and red.
KW.meaning: Pan-Arab colors. Green is the fields, white our deeds, red our swords, and black our battles — a line of poetry often used to explain the flag.

KG.design: A red field with a gold sun whose center is a stylized yurt crown (tunduk).
KG.meaning: Red is bravery and the flag of the national hero Manas. The sun is peace and wealth. The tunduk is the circular roof frame of a yurt — home, the sky, and the universe in one emblem. Rays were redrawn in 2023 to look less like a sunflower.

colors.name: Gold
colors.meaning: The sun and the yurt crown

KG.emblem: A 40-ray sun around a yurt tunduk; forty rays are the forty tribes of the Manas epic.

LA.design: Three horizontal bands of red, blue (double width), and red with a white disc in the center.
LA.meaning: Red is the blood of independence. Blue is the Mekong and prosperity. The white disc is the full moon over the Mekong and the unity of the people under communism.

colors.name: White
colors.meaning: The moon, and a united people

LA.emblem: A white full-moon disc, replacing the old three-headed elephant of the kingdom.

LV.design: A deep carmine field with a narrow white stripe through the center.
LV.meaning: Legend says a wounded Latvian chief was wrapped in a white sheet; the edges soaked with blood, the middle stayed white. Carmine is darker than most red flags. The design is mentioned in medieval chronicles.

colors.name: Carmine
colors.meaning: The blood of a wounded leader

LB.design: Two red bands around a white band holding a green cedar tree.
LB.meaning: Red is sacrifice, white peace and the snow of the mountains. The cedar is holiness, eternity, and Lebanon itself — a tree mentioned in ancient texts and still growing in the high groves.
LB.emblem: A cedar tree, the national tree and the heart of the flag.

LS.design: Three horizontal bands of blue, white, and green with a black mokorotlo (Basotho hat) in the center.
LS.meaning: Blue is rain and the sky, white peace, green prosperity. The conical hat is a national dress item and a symbol of the Basotho people, replacing an earlier military emblem.
LS.emblem: A mokorotlo, the traditional Basotho hat.

LR.design: Eleven red and white stripes with a blue canton holding a single white star.
LR.meaning: Modeled on the U.S. flag by freed American settlers. Eleven stripes are the signers of the independence declaration. The lone star is the then-only independent African republic.
LR.emblem: A single white star, the “Lone Star of Africa.”

LY.design: Three horizontal bands of red, black (double width), and green with a white crescent and star on the black band.
LY.meaning: The 1951 independence flag, restored after 2011. Red is the blood of freedom, black the dark years of Italian occupation, green wealth and Islam. The crescent and star are Islam.
LY.emblem: A crescent and star on the wide black band.

LI.design: Two horizontal bands of blue and red with a gold crown at the upper hoist.
LI.meaning: Blue is the sky, red the evening fires in the homes of the people. The crown was added after the 1936 Olympics, when Liechtenstein discovered its flag matched Haiti’s; the crown marks a principality.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The hearth fires of the people

LI.emblem: A gold crown, added so the flag would not be confused with Haiti’s.

LT.design: Three equal horizontal bands of yellow, green, and red.
LT.meaning: Yellow is the sun and wheat, green the forests, red the blood of those who defended the country. Revived with independence from the Soviet Union.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: Courage and the blood of defenders

LU.design: Three equal horizontal bands of red, white, and light blue.
LU.meaning: The same layout as the Netherlands, but with a lighter blue so the two flags can be told apart. The colors come from the grand duke’s arms: a red lion on blue-and-white stripes.

colors.name: White
colors.meaning: The striped field of the arms

colors.name: Light blue
colors.meaning: The striped field, in a sky-blue shade

LU.coatOfArms: A red lion on barred blue and white — the flag flattened those arms into three stripes.

MO.design: A green field with a white lotus above a stylized bridge and water, under five yellow stars.
MO.meaning: Green sets Macau apart from China’s red. The lotus is the city’s flower. The bridge and water are the territory’s harbor. Five stars echo China’s flag and the link to the motherland.

colors.name: Green
colors.meaning: Macau as a special administrative region

MO.emblem: A lotus, bridge, and five stars — the same design as the regional emblem.

MG.design: A white vertical band at the hoist and two horizontal bands of red and green.
MG.meaning: White and red are the colors of the Merina kingdom. Green was added for hope and the coastal peoples, so the flag would speak for the whole island.

MW.design: Three horizontal bands of black, red, and green with a red rising sun on the black band.
MW.meaning: Black is the people of Africa, red the blood of freedom, green the land. The rising sun is a new dawn — Malawi means “flames” in Chichewa, a name for the sun on Lake Malawi.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The blood of the freedom struggle

MW.emblem: A red rising sun with 31 rays.

MY.design: Fourteen red and white stripes with a blue canton holding a gold crescent and a 14-point star.
MY.meaning: Stripes and points are the 13 states plus the federal government. The crescent is Islam; the star is unity. Red, white, and blue nod to the U.S. and British flags that influenced the design.

colors.name: Red and white
colors.meaning: The equal states of the federation

colors.name: Gold
colors.meaning: Royalty, the crescent, and the star

MY.emblem: A crescent and the 14-point Federal Star.

MV.design: A red field with a green rectangle and a white crescent in the center.
MV.meaning: Red is the blood of heroes. Green is peace and the abundant palm trees. The crescent is Islam, the state religion.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The blood of those who defended the nation

ML.design: A vertical tricolor of green, yellow, and red.
ML.meaning: Pan-African colors. Green is the land, yellow purity and mineral wealth, red the blood of those who died for independence. A first version had a human figure (kanaga); it was dropped as too figurative for some Muslim leaders.

MT.design: A vertical bicolor of white and red with the George Cross in a red-edged canton.
MT.meaning: White and red are a medieval legend of a Norman count’s banner. The George Cross was awarded to the whole island by King George VI in 1942 for bravery under siege in World War II — a medal worn on the flag.
MT.emblem: The George Cross, a British medal made into a national charge.

MH.design: A blue field with a rising diagonal of white and orange and a 24-point star at the upper hoist.
MH.meaning: Blue is the Pacific. The diagonal is the equator; white is the Ratak (sunrise) chain, orange the Ralik (sunset) chain. The star’s 24 points are the municipalities; the four long rays are the main centers.

MQ.design: A red triangle at the hoist and two horizontal bands of green and black.
MQ.meaning: The “red, green, and black” flag of Martinican identity, long used by cultural movements and made official in 2023. Green is the land, black the people, red the blood shared by all. France’s tricolor remains the national flag.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The blood and vitality of the people

MR.design: A green field with a gold crescent and star, and red stripes at the top and bottom.
MR.meaning: Green and the crescent-star pair are Islam. Gold is the Sahara. Red stripes added in 2017 honor those who died for the country.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The blood of those who defended the nation

MU.design: Four equal horizontal bands of red, blue, yellow, and green.
MU.meaning: Red is independence, blue the Indian Ocean, yellow the light of independence, and green the lush vegetation of the island.

YT.design: A white field with the unofficial coat of arms — two seahorses, a rising crescent, and the words “Ra Hachiri.” The official flag is the French tricolor.
YT.meaning: Mayotte is a French department. Local banners use seahorses for the sea, a crescent for the Muslim majority, and a motto meaning “We are vigilant.”

colors.name: White
colors.meaning: The field of the local arms banner

colors.name: Blue and red
colors.meaning: Details in the unofficial arms, and France

YT.coatOfArms: Two seahorses supporting a shield with a crescent — a local emblem, not an official national coat of arms.

MX.design: A vertical tricolor of green, white, and red with the coat of arms on the white band.
MX.meaning: The colors began as independence-army colors. Today green is hope, white unity, and red the blood of heroes. The emblem is the Aztec founding omen of Tenochtitlan, now Mexico City.
MX.emblem: An eagle on a cactus eating a serpent.
MX.coatOfArms: The flag is built around the coat of arms: the eagle-and-serpent vision that told the Mexica where to build their capital. Italy’s similar tricolor has no emblem, which is how the two are told apart.

FM.design: A light-blue field with four white stars in a diamond.
FM.meaning: Blue is the Pacific. Four stars are the four states: Yap, Chuuk, Pohnpei, and Kosrae. A quiet flag with no canton or Union Jack, marking a break from the Trust Territory design.

colors.name: White
colors.meaning: Peace, and the four state stars

FM.emblem: Four stars for the four states.

MD.design: A vertical tricolor of blue, yellow, and red with the coat of arms on the yellow band.
MD.meaning: The same colors as Romania, Moldova’s cultural neighbor. The arms — an eagle holding an Orthodox cross, olive, and scepter, with an aurochs shield — are what make the flag Moldovan.

colors.name: Yellow
colors.meaning: The land and the band that holds the arms

MD.coatOfArms: A Roman eagle with an aurochs-head shield, the medieval symbol of Moldavia. The flag is those arms on the Romanian tricolor.

MC.design: Two equal horizontal bands of red and white.
MC.meaning: Red and white are the heraldic colors of the Grimaldi family, who have ruled Monaco for centuries. The same colors as Indonesia, in a shorter, squarer flag.
MC.coatOfArms: Lozenges of red and white; the flag simplifies that pattern into two bands.

MN.design: Three vertical bands of red, blue, and red with a gold Soyombo emblem at the hoist.
MN.meaning: Blue is the eternal sky, sacred in Mongol tradition. Red is progress and prosperity. The Soyombo is a national script-symbol: fire, sun, moon, earth, water, and the yin-yang of two fish.
MN.emblem: The Soyombo, a stacked emblem unique to Mongolia.

ME.design: A red field with a gold border and the coat of arms — a double-headed eagle — in the center.
ME.meaning: Red and gold are historic Montenegrin royal colors. The two-headed eagle looks east and west, a Byzantine emblem used by the Petrović-Njegoš dynasty.
ME.coatOfArms: A gold double-headed eagle with a lion on its chest — the flag is a banner of these arms.

MS.design: A British Blue Ensign with a shield of Erin (a woman with a harp) and the cross of St. Patrick, recalling Irish settlers.
MS.meaning: The Union Jack marks a British overseas territory. The Irish figure and harp remember the Irish indentured servants who named the island after a harbor in Spain, but whose culture shaped the badge.
MS.coatOfArms: A woman with a cross and harp beside a hill and a broken cross — the Irish-themed arms in the fly.

MA.design: A red field with a green pentagram, the Seal of Solomon, in the center.
MA.meaning: Red is the Alaouite dynasty. The five-pointed green star is the seal of Solomon and the five pillars of Islam, added in 1915 so the plain red flag would not be confused with other red banners.

colors.name: Green
colors.meaning: Islam, and the Seal of Solomon

MZ.design: Green, black, and yellow horizontal bands edged in white, with a red hoist triangle holding a book, hoe, and AK-47 over a star.
MZ.meaning: Green is the land, black Africa, yellow minerals, white peace, and red the independence war. The rifle, hoe, and book are defense, farming, and education — one of the few national flags that shows a modern firearm.
MZ.emblem: A star, book, hoe, and Kalashnikov, the emblem of the independence movement.

MM.design: Three horizontal bands of yellow, green, and red with a large white star in the center.
MM.meaning: Yellow is solidarity, green peace and the land, red courage. The white star is the union of the country. The design replaced a socialist-era flag with a cogwheel and rice.

NA.design: A red diagonal stripe edged in white between a blue triangle with a gold sun and a green triangle.
NA.meaning: Blue is the sky and the Atlantic. The sun is life and energy. White is peace, red the people and their heroism, and green the land. Designed for independence from South Africa.
NA.emblem: A twelve-ray gold sun in the upper hoist.

NR.design: A blue field with a thin gold stripe and a white 12-point star below the stripe toward the hoist.
NR.meaning: Blue is the Pacific. The gold line is the equator; the star sits just below it because Nauru is a degree south of the equator. Twelve points are the twelve original tribes.

colors.name: White
colors.meaning: The star of the twelve tribes

NR.emblem: A 12-point star placed just under the equator line.

NP.design: The world’s only non-rectangular national flag: two stacked crimson pennants with a blue border, a white moon above a white sun.
NP.meaning: Crimson is the national color. Blue is peace. The moon and sun mean the nation should last as long as those bodies. The double-pennant shape comes from Himalayan war banners.

colors.name: Crimson
colors.meaning: The rhododendron and the national color

colors.name: White
colors.meaning: The moon and sun, and purity

NP.emblem: A crescent moon and a sun with a face, simplified in 1962 from earlier human-faced versions.

NL.design: Three equal horizontal bands of red, white, and blue.
NL.meaning: The Prince’s Flag of the Dutch Revolt was orange-white-blue. Orange faded and was replaced by red, which showed better at sea. It became a model for the Russian and later many Slavic flags.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: A practical replacement for the original orange

colors.name: White
colors.meaning: The middle band of the Prince’s Flag

colors.name: Blue
colors.meaning: The lower band of the Prince’s Flag

NC.design: A blue-red-green tricolor with a yellow disc and a flèche faîtière — the Kanak independence flag, flown beside the French tricolor.
NC.meaning: Blue is the sky, red the blood and unity of the people, green the land. The yellow disc is the sun; the flèche faîtière is a carved rooftop spire of a Kanak house, a symbol of the indigenous people.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: Blood and the unity of Kanak clans

NC.emblem: A flèche faîtière on a sun disc, the Kanak rooftop carving.

NZ.design: A Blue Ensign with the Southern Cross in the fly, the four main stars in red outlined in white.
NZ.meaning: The Union Jack records British heritage. The Southern Cross is the sky over New Zealand, drawn in red to differ from Australia’s white stars. A 2016 referendum kept this flag.

colors.name: Blue
colors.meaning: The sea and sky, on a Blue Ensign

NZ.emblem: The four main stars of Crux, plus a smaller fifth star.

NI.design: Three horizontal bands of blue, white, and blue with the coat of arms in the center.
NI.meaning: Blue is the two oceans and justice; white is peace. The triangle of volcanoes is the old Federal Republic of Central America, still living on this flag.

colors.name: Blue
colors.meaning: The Atlantic and Pacific, and justice

NI.coatOfArms: A triangle with five volcanoes, a rainbow, and a cap of liberty — the flag always shows these arms.

NE.design: Three horizontal bands of orange, white, and green with an orange disc in the center.
NE.meaning: Orange is the Sahara in the north. White is purity and the Niger River. Green is the fertile south. The disc is the sun, or independence.

NG.design: Three vertical bands of green, white, and green.
NG.meaning: Green is the forests and agriculture. White is peace and unity — a simple design chosen from a national contest at independence, by student Michael Taiwo Akinkunmi.

NU.design: A yellow field with a Union Jack canton; the canton holds a gold disc, four stars, and a larger central star.
NU.meaning: Yellow is the bright sunshine of Niue and the warmth of its people toward New Zealand. The stars are Niue (center) and the Southern Cross, on a Union Jack that records the realm link.

colors.name: Yellow
colors.meaning: Sunshine and friendship with New Zealand

NU.emblem: A gold disc and five stars on the Union Jack.

NF.design: A green-white-green vertical triband with a green Norfolk Island pine in the center.
NF.meaning: Green is the island’s vegetation. The pine — Araucaria heterophylla — is the island’s famous tree, used for masts in the sailing age and still the local emblem.

colors.name: White
colors.meaning: The band that holds the pine

KP.design: A wide red band edged in white between two blue bands, with a white disc and a red star at the hoist.
KP.meaning: Red is revolutionary tradition. White is purity, ancient Korean culture, and the white-clad people. Blue is sovereignty, peace, and friendship. The star is socialism.
KP.emblem: A red star in a white disc.

MK.design: A red field with a gold eight-ray sun whose rays reach the edges.
MK.meaning: The sun is liberty and the “new sun of liberty” in the national anthem. An earlier Vergina Sun design was changed after a dispute with Greece; this stylized sun settled the issue.
MK.emblem: An eight-ray sun filling the flag.

MP.design: A blue field with a white star over a gray latte stone, ringed by a mwarmwar (floral head wreath).
MP.meaning: Blue is the Pacific and the Marianas. The star is the commonwealth. The latte stone is an ancient Chamorro house pillar. The wreath is Carolinian culture — two peoples on one flag.
MP.emblem: A star, latte stone, and mwarmwar wreath — the commonwealth seal.

NO.design: A red field with a blue Nordic cross outlined in white.
NO.meaning: Red and white come from Denmark, Norway’s former partner. Blue was added to sit among the French and American flags admired by the designer, and to differ from Denmark. The off-center cross is the Nordic family mark.

colors.name: Blue
colors.meaning: Independence, and a link to other free flags

NO.emblem: A Nordic cross in red, white, and blue.

OM.design: A vertical red band at the hoist with the national emblem, and three horizontal bands of white, red, and green.
OM.meaning: White is peace and prosperity, red the battles fought to keep the country free, green the Jebel Akhdar and fertility. The emblem is two crossed swords, a dagger (khanjar), and a belt — Omani ceremonial arms.
OM.emblem: A khanjar dagger over crossed swords.
OM.coatOfArms: That same khanjar badge is the national emblem, placed at the top of the red hoist.

PK.design: A dark-green field with a white hoist stripe, a white crescent, and a five-pointed star.
PK.meaning: Green and the crescent-star pair are Islam, the majority faith. The white stripe is the religious minorities and their equal rights. The star is light and knowledge.

colors.name: White
colors.meaning: Minorities, peace, and the crescent and star

PK.emblem: A crescent and star, slightly tilted.

PW.design: A light-blue field with a gold disc slightly toward the hoist.
PW.meaning: Blue is the Pacific. The gold disc is the full moon, the best time in Palauan tradition to harvest, celebrate, and begin new work — not the sun, unlike Japan’s similar flag.
PW.emblem: A full moon, offset like Bangladesh’s sun so it looks centered in the wind.

PS.design: Black, white, and green horizontal bands with a red triangle at the hoist.
PS.meaning: The Pan-Arab colors of the 1916 Arab Revolt, used by Palestinian nationalism since the 1960s. Black, white, and green are historic caliphates; red is the Hashemite and Arab-Revolt color.

PA.design: Four quarters: white with a blue star, red, blue, and white with a red star.
PA.meaning: Blue is the Conservative Party, red the Liberal Party, and white the peace that should hold them together. The stars are purity and law. Designed at independence from Colombia in 1903.
PA.emblem: Two stars, one blue and one red.

PG.design: A diagonal bicolor of black and red with the Southern Cross in white and a gold bird-of-paradise.
PG.meaning: Black, red, and gold are traditional colors in many Papua New Guinean cultures. The Southern Cross is the sky; the bird-of-paradise is the national bird, shown in flight.

colors.name: Black
colors.meaning: A traditional color, and the night sky

PG.emblem: The Southern Cross and a raggiana bird-of-paradise.

PY.design: Three horizontal bands of red, white, and blue — the only national flag with a different emblem on each side.
PY.meaning: The colors nod to the French tricolor and independence ideals. The obverse shows the star of May and a lion; the reverse shows a treasury seal. Red is patriotism, white honesty, blue liberty.
