PY.emblem: A star in a wreath on the front; a lion and the words Paz y Justicia on the back.
PY.coatOfArms: Two different seals, one per side — unique among national flags.

PE.design: A vertical tricolor of red, white, and red. The state flag adds the coat of arms on the white band.
PE.meaning: Legend says José de San Martín saw flamingos — red and white — as a good omen. Red is the blood of freedom; white is peace and dignity.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The blood of the independence fighters

PE.coatOfArms: A vicuña, a cinchona tree, and a cornucopia — animals, medicine, and mineral wealth — used on the state flag.

PH.design: A white triangle at the hoist with a gold sun and three stars, and horizontal bands of blue and red that swap in wartime.
PH.meaning: The sun’s eight rays are the first eight provinces to revolt against Spain. Three stars are Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao. Blue is peace, red valor; in war the red band is flown on top.
PH.emblem: An eight-ray sun and three stars.

PN.design: A British Blue Ensign with a shield of the Bible, an anchor, and a flowering plant, plus a Pitcairn wheelbarrow and a miro sprig.
PN.meaning: The Union Jack marks a British territory. The badge tells the Bounty story: an anchor for the ship, a Bible for the mutineers’ faith, and a wheelbarrow for the islanders’ work.

colors.name: Blue
colors.meaning: The Pacific, on a Blue Ensign

PN.coatOfArms: The fly shield is the coat of arms granted in 1969.

PL.design: Two equal horizontal bands of white and red.
PL.meaning: White and red come from the arms: a white eagle on a red shield. White is the eagle; red is the field. A simple bicolor that reads as the arms without drawing the bird.
PL.coatOfArms: The White Eagle appears on the state flag with arms; the civil flag is the plain bicolor.

PT.design: A green hoist and a red fly with the armillary sphere and shield at the color divide.
PT.meaning: Green is hope and the republican revolution of 1910; red is the blood of the people. The armillary sphere is the Age of Discovery. The shield’s seven castles and five bezants are medieval Portugal.
PT.emblem: An armillary sphere behind the national shield.
PT.coatOfArms: The flag carries the lesser arms: sphere plus the quinas shield, without the two castles of the greater arms.

PR.design: Five red and white stripes with a blue hoist triangle holding a white star — a cousin of Cuba’s flag with the colors swapped.
PR.meaning: Designed in 1895 by independence exiles in New York. Stripes are the original five departments. The triangle is the republican ideals; the star is the island. Blue shade has varied between sky and navy.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The blood of those who fought for the island

PR.emblem: A single white star in a triangle.

QA.design: A maroon field with a white serrated hoist, nine white points — the only national flag that is more than twice as long as it is tall.
QA.meaning: Maroon (a dye that darkened in the sun) sets Qatar apart from Bahrain’s red. White is peace. Nine points are sometimes linked to Qatar as the ninth emirate in a 1916 British treaty count.

colors.name: Maroon
colors.meaning: A distinctive Qatari dye, darker than neighboring reds

QA.emblem: Nine white serrations along the hoist.

RE.design: A widely used local flag shows a volcano and sunbursts on blue and red; the official flag is the French tricolor.
RE.meaning: Réunion is a French department. The popular Lö Mahavéli flag uses the Piton de la Fournaise volcano and radiating colors for the island’s cultures. France’s tricolor remains official.

colors.name: Blue
colors.meaning: The sky and the Indian Ocean on the local design

colors.name: Red and gold
colors.meaning: The volcano and the sun on the local design

RE.emblem: Piton de la Fournaise, the island’s active volcano, on unofficial flags.

RO.design: A vertical tricolor of blue, yellow, and red.
RO.meaning: Blue is the sky, yellow justice and the fields, red the blood of the people — a reading from the 19th century. The communist coat of arms that once sat in the center was cut out during the 1989 revolution.

colors.name: Yellow
colors.meaning: Justice and the wealth of the land

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: Fraternity and the blood of the people

RU.design: Three equal horizontal bands of white, blue, and red.
RU.meaning: Peter the Great took the Dutch tricolor and reordered it for his navy. White, blue, and red later became the pan-Slavic colors. Restored after the Soviet red banner.

colors.name: White
colors.meaning: Nobility and frankness in older readings

RW.design: A wide blue band over thinner yellow and green bands, with a gold sun in the upper fly.
RW.meaning: Blue is peace and happiness, yellow economic development, green hope and prosperity. The sun is a new era after the 1994 genocide — a deliberate break from the older red-yellow-green flag.

colors.name: Gold
colors.meaning: The sun of a new era

BL.design: A white field with the island’s coat of arms; the official flag is the French tricolor.
BL.meaning: Saint Barthélemy is a French collectivity. Local banners show the Maltese cross and mural crown of the arms, recalling the Knights of Malta who once held the island, and the three crowns of Sweden, another former ruler.

colors.name: White
colors.meaning: The field of the unofficial arms banner

BL.coatOfArms: A shield with a Maltese cross, three gold crowns, and the fleur-de-lis of France — history stacked in one badge.

SH.design: A British Blue Ensign with a shield of a sailing ship and a Saint Helena plover (wirebird) on the shore.
SH.meaning: The Union Jack marks a British overseas territory. The ship is the East India Company vessel that found the island; the wirebird is endemic to Saint Helena.

colors.name: Blue
colors.meaning: The South Atlantic, on a Blue Ensign

SH.coatOfArms: The fly shield is the coat of arms: a ship near the rocky shore and a wirebird.

KN.design: Green and red triangles divided by a black diagonal stripe edged in yellow, with two white stars on the black.
KN.meaning: Green is the land, red the struggle, yellow sunshine, and black the African heritage of the people. Two stars are hope and liberty, and the two islands.

colors.name: Black
colors.meaning: The African heritage of the people

colors.name: White
colors.meaning: The two stars of hope and liberty

KN.emblem: Two white stars on the black diagonal.

LC.design: A cerulean field with a gold triangle over a black-edged white triangle — a simplified Piton.
LC.meaning: Blue is the sky and sea. The triangles are the Pitons, the twin volcanic spires of the island. Gold is sunshine and prosperity; black and white are the two races living in unity.

colors.name: White
colors.meaning: Purity, and living together in unity

LC.emblem: A stylized pair of Pitons, the island’s famous peaks.

MF.design: A white field with a local coat of arms is sometimes seen; the official flag is the French tricolor.
MF.meaning: French Saint Martin is a collectivity. It has no official separate flag. Local civic arms may show a ship, a palm, and the island’s name, but France’s tricolor is the flag of state.

colors.name: Blue, white, and red
colors.meaning: The French tricolor, the official flag

PM.design: A blue ship on a white-and-blue sea, with Basque, Breton, and Norman flags in the hoist — a popular local banner. Officially the French tricolor flies.
PM.meaning: The ship is the Grande Hermine, which brought Jacques Cartier. The three regional flags honor the Basque, Breton, and Norman sailors who settled the islands.
PM.emblem: A 16th-century ship and three European regional flags.
PM.coatOfArms: The unofficial flag is a banner of the unofficial arms.

VC.design: A vertical tricolor of blue, gold (wider), and green with three green diamonds in a V on the gold band.
VC.meaning: Blue is the sky and sea. Gold is sunshine, warm sand, and the bright spirit of the people. Green is lush vegetation and vitality. The diamonds — “the Gems” — replaced the coat of arms so the flag would read clearly at a distance.

colors.name: Blue
colors.meaning: The sky and the Caribbean Sea

colors.name: Gold
colors.meaning: Sunshine, golden sand, and a bright spirit

colors.name: Green
colors.meaning: The islands’ vegetation and the vitality of Vincentians

VC.emblem: Three green diamonds in a V for Vincent, and for the nickname “Gems of the Antilles.”
VC.coatOfArms: The 1979 independence flag put the coat of arms on a breadfruit leaf. In 1985 those arms — two women at an altar, a cotton plant, and the motto Pax et Justitia (“Peace and Justice”) — were replaced by the three diamonds, which are easier to see from far away.

WS.design: A red field with a blue canton holding the Southern Cross in white.
WS.meaning: Red is courage. Blue is freedom. White is purity. The Southern Cross is the sky over Samoa, a design kept from the New Zealand trusteeship into independence.
WS.emblem: The five stars of the Southern Cross.

SM.design: Two horizontal bands of white and light blue with the coat of arms in the center.
SM.meaning: White is snow on Mount Titano and peace. Blue is the sky. The arms show three towers on the mountain — Guaita, Cesta, and Montale — the fortress-republic in one picture.
SM.coatOfArms: Three towers with ostrich-feather weathervanes, a crown, and the motto Libertas. The civil flag may omit the arms; the state flag shows them.

ST.design: Horizontal bands of green, yellow, and green with a red triangle at the hoist and two black stars on the yellow.
ST.meaning: Pan-African colors. Green is the land, yellow the cocoa of the islands, red the struggle. Two stars are São Tomé and Príncipe.
ST.emblem: Two black stars for the two islands.

SA.design: A green field with the Shahada in white thuluth script and a white sword below.
SA.meaning: Green is Islam. The inscription is “There is no god but God; Muhammad is the messenger of God.” The sword is justice and the founding House of Saud. Because it bears the creed, the flag is never flown at half-mast.
SA.emblem: The Islamic creed and a straight sword.
SA.coatOfArms: The national emblem is two crossed swords and a palm; the flag uses one sword and the Shahada instead.

SN.design: A vertical tricolor of green, yellow, and red with a green star in the center.
SN.meaning: Pan-African colors shared with Mali, the former federation partner. Green is hope and Islam, yellow wealth, red sacrifice. The star is unity and a guiding light.

RS.design: A horizontal tricolor of red, blue, and white with the lesser coat of arms toward the hoist.
RS.meaning: Pan-Slavic colors in the Serbian order (red-blue-white). The arms are a white cross on red with four firesteels — often read as four C’s — and a crown.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: A pan-Slavic color, and the Serbian shield

colors.name: White
colors.meaning: A pan-Slavic color, and the cross

RS.coatOfArms: A crowned double-headed eagle with the Serbian cross on its chest — the flag carries the lesser version of these arms.

SC.design: Five rays from the lower hoist: blue, yellow, red, white, and green.
SC.meaning: A rising fan of colors for a new coalition era. Blue is the sky and sea, yellow the sun, red the people, white social justice, and green the land.

colors.name: Green
colors.meaning: The land and the natural environment

SL.design: Three equal horizontal bands of green, white, and blue.
SL.meaning: Green is the agriculture and mountains. White is unity and justice. Blue is the natural harbor of Freetown, the reason the settlement was founded.

SG.design: Two horizontal bands of red and white with a white crescent and five stars at the upper hoist.
SG.meaning: Red is universal brotherhood and equality. White is purity and virtue. The crescent is a young nation; five stars are democracy, peace, progress, justice, and equality.
SG.emblem: A crescent and five stars, also used as the national coat of arms charges.

SX.design: Two horizontal bands of red and blue with a white triangle at the hoist holding the coat of arms.
SX.meaning: Red is solidarity, blue the sea and peace, white the promise of a bright future. The arms show a monument, a badge of the island, and the motto Semper pro grediens (“Always progressing”).
SX.coatOfArms: A shield with a brown pelican, a monument, and a courthouse, on the white triangle.

SK.design: A horizontal tricolor of white, blue, and red with the coat of arms toward the hoist.
SK.meaning: Pan-Slavic colors. The arms are a double cross on three blue hills — the patriarchal cross of Byzantine missionaries, standing on Tatra, Fatra, and Mátra.

colors.name: Blue
colors.meaning: A pan-Slavic color, and the three hills

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: A pan-Slavic color, and the shield

SK.coatOfArms: A white double cross on three blue hills, placed on the tricolor so Slovakia is not confused with Russia.

SI.design: A horizontal tricolor of white, blue, and red with the coat of arms in the upper hoist.
SI.meaning: The same Slavic tricolor as Slovakia and Russia. The arms — Triglav, the highest peak, under stars from the Counts of Celje, over wavy water — make it Slovenian.

colors.name: White
colors.meaning: A pan-Slavic color, and the mountain snow

colors.name: Blue
colors.meaning: A pan-Slavic color, and the sky and sea

SI.coatOfArms: Mount Triglav, three gold stars, and two wavy blue lines for the sea and rivers.

SB.design: A thin yellow diagonal from lower hoist to upper fly, with blue above (five white stars) and green below.
SB.meaning: Blue is the water, green the land, yellow the sun. Five stars were the original five districts.
SB.emblem: Five white stars for the first five districts.

SO.design: A light-blue field with a single white five-pointed star.
SO.meaning: Blue was taken from the United Nations flag, under whose trusteeship the design was born. The star’s five points are the five regions where Somalis live: British Somaliland, Italian Somaliland, French Somaliland (Djibouti), the Ogaden, and northern Kenya.

colors.name: Light blue
colors.meaning: The United Nations, and the sky

colors.name: White
colors.meaning: Peace and the Star of Unity

ZA.design: A horizontal Y of green edged in gold, splitting a red upper band and a blue lower band, with a black triangle at the hoist edged in white.
ZA.meaning: The Y is convergence — many paths becoming one. Black, green, and gold come from the ANC; red, white, and blue from older Boer and British flags. Together they are a new nation, not a winner’s banner.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: Bloodshed and the older republican flags

colors.name: Blue
colors.meaning: The sky and the older flags

colors.name: White
colors.meaning: The European heritage flags, and peace

GS.design: A British Blue Ensign with a shield of a lion, a torch, and fur seals, supported by a fur seal and a macaroni penguin.
GS.meaning: The Union Jack marks a British overseas territory. The torch is exploration; the animals are the wildlife of South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands.

colors.name: Blue
colors.meaning: The Southern Ocean, on a Blue Ensign

GS.coatOfArms: The full arms in the fly, with seal and penguin supporters — one of the most crowded territorial badges.

KR.design: A white field with a red-and-blue taegeuk and four black trigrams in the corners.
KR.meaning: White is the traditional Korean color of peace and the people. The taegeuk is yin and yang in balance. The four trigrams are heaven, earth, water, and fire — a flag of philosophy more than of a dynasty.
KR.emblem: The taegeuk and the four gua from the I Ching.

SS.design: Black, red, and green bands edged in white, with a blue hoist triangle holding a gold star.
SS.meaning: Black is the people, red the blood of freedom, green the land, white peace. Blue is the Nile; the gold star is the Star of Bethlehem, a guide for the new nation.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The blood of the independence struggle

SS.emblem: A gold star in a blue triangle.

ES.design: Three horizontal bands of red, gold (double width), and red with the coat of arms toward the hoist.
ES.meaning: Red and gold are the colors of the Crowns of Castile and Aragon. The arms quarter those kingdoms plus Navarre, Granada, and the Bourbon fleurs-de-lis, under a crown and the Pillars of Hercules.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: Castile and the historic Spanish banner

ES.coatOfArms: A quartered shield of the historic kingdoms, the Pillars of Hercules, and the motto Plus Ultra — the flag is those arms on the rojigualda.

LK.design: A gold field with two vertical stripes of green and orange and a maroon rectangle holding a gold lion with a sword, four bo leaves at the corners.
LK.meaning: The lion is the Sinhalese people and the legendary first king. Orange is the Tamil community, green the Moor community. Bo leaves are Buddhism. Maroon is the historic Sinhalese royal color.

colors.name: Gold
colors.meaning: The border, the lion, and the bo leaves

LK.emblem: The lion of Lanka holding a kastane sword.
LK.coatOfArms: The lion banner is older than the modern coat of arms; the flag is a living royal emblem, not a later seal.

SD.design: Red, white, and black horizontal bands with a green triangle at the hoist.
SD.meaning: Arab Liberation colors. Red is the struggle, white peace and optimism, black the name Sudan (“land of the blacks”) and the Mahdist past, green Islam and agriculture.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The struggle and socialism of the era

colors.name: Black
colors.meaning: The name Sudan and the Mahdist banner

SR.design: Green, white, red (wide), white, and green bands with a gold star on the red.
SR.meaning: Green is the forests, white justice and freedom, red progress and the people. The gold star is a united, golden future.

SJ.design: The flag of Norway: a red field with a blue Nordic cross outlined in white.
SJ.meaning: Svalbard and Jan Mayen are parts of Norway, so they fly the Norwegian flag. There is no separate territorial ensign.

SE.design: A blue field with a gold Nordic cross.
SE.meaning: Blue and gold come from the 14th-century royal arms: three gold crowns on blue. Legend also ties the cross to King Eric IX seeing a gold cross in the blue sky. Offset like other Nordic flags.

colors.name: Blue
colors.meaning: The field of the royal arms

SE.emblem: A Nordic cross in the royal colors.
SE.coatOfArms: Three gold crowns on blue — the flag is those colors laid out as a cross.

CH.design: A red square with a bold white cross in the center.
CH.meaning: The white cross on red comes from the Holy Roman Empire’s war flag and from Schwyz, a founding canton. Square, unlike most flags. The Red Cross later reversed these colors as a tribute to Swiss neutrality.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The field of Schwyz and the old imperial war flag

colors.name: White
colors.meaning: The Christian cross of the confederates

CH.emblem: A Greek cross (equal arms) rather than a Nordic one.

SY.design: Three horizontal bands of green, white, and black with three red stars on the white band.
SY.meaning: The independence flag of 1932, used by the opposition and made official in March 2025 after the Assad government fell. Green, white, and black are the older Arab-kingdom colors; three red stars were the original districts of Aleppo, Damascus, and Deir ez-Zor.

colors.name: Green
colors.meaning: The Hashemite Arab kingdom colors, and hope

colors.name: White
colors.meaning: Peace, and the band that holds the stars

colors.name: Black
colors.meaning: The darker past, and the Abbasid color

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The three historic districts, in the stars

SY.emblem: Three red stars for the original Syrian districts, replacing the two green stars of the 1980–2024 flag.

TW.design: A red field with a blue canton holding a white 12-ray sun.
TW.meaning: The “Blue Sky, White Sun, and a Wholly Red Earth” of the Republic of China. Blue is nationalism and liberty, white the sun of progress (12 rays for the hours), red the blood of the revolution and fraternity.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The earth and the blood of the revolution

TW.emblem: A 12-ray white sun, also the emblem of the Kuomintang.

TJ.design: Three horizontal bands of red, white (wider), and green with a gold crown and seven stars on the white.
TJ.meaning: Red is the sun, victory, and the workers. White is cotton and the snow of the mountains. Green is Islam and the valleys. The crown and seven stars are the state, the seven ancient regions, and a verse of the Qur’an about seven heavens.

TZ.design: A green triangle and a blue triangle divided by a black diagonal edged in yellow.
TZ.meaning: Green is the land, blue the lakes and Indian Ocean, black the people, and yellow mineral wealth. The diagonal unites Tanganyika and Zanzibar in one flag.

TH.design: Five horizontal stripes of red, white, blue (double width), white, and red — the Trairanga.
TH.meaning: Red is the land and the people, white Buddhism and religion, blue the monarchy. Blue was added during World War I to stand with the Allies and to honor King Vajiravudh’s color.

TL.design: A red field with a black triangle edged in yellow at the hoist, holding a white star.
TL.meaning: Red is the struggle for freedom. Yellow is the country’s wealth. Black is the dark centuries that must be overcome. The white star is peace, guiding the way.

colors.name: Black
colors.meaning: The darkness to be left behind

TL.emblem: A white star on the black triangle.

TG.design: Five green and yellow stripes with a red canton holding a white star.
TG.meaning: Pan-African colors. Green is hope and agriculture, yellow mineral wealth, red blood and loyalty. Five stripes are the regions. The white star is purity and life.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: Charity, fidelity, and the blood of the struggle

TG.emblem: A white star in a red canton.

TK.design: A blue field with a yellow Tokelauan canoe sailing toward the Southern Cross.
TK.meaning: Blue is the Pacific. The canoe is the community’s voyage toward the best way to govern itself. The Southern Cross is the sky that guides Tokelau, a territory of New Zealand.

colors.name: Yellow
colors.meaning: The canoe and the Southern Cross, for Christianity and a guiding sky

TK.emblem: A traditional canoe and four Southern Cross stars.

TO.design: A red field with a white canton holding a red cross.
TO.meaning: Red is the blood of Christ; the cross is Christianity, the state religion. King George Tupou I wanted a flag that would not be confused with the Red Cross, so the cross sits in a white canton rather than filling the flag.
TO.emblem: A red Greek cross in the canton.

TT.design: A red field with a black diagonal stripe edged in white from upper hoist to lower fly.
TT.meaning: Red is the people, the sun, and the warmth of the land. Black is the earth and strength. White is the sea and the equality of all. A “color over color” design with no emblem.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The people and the sun’s warmth

TN.design: A red field with a white disc holding a red crescent and star.
TN.meaning: Red comes from the Ottoman flag used when Tunisia was an autonomous province. The crescent and star are Islam. The white disc sets it apart from Turkey’s flag.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The blood of martyrs, and the Ottoman heritage

colors.name: White
colors.meaning: Peace, and the disc behind the crescent

TN.emblem: A crescent and star, the same pair as on the coat of arms.

TR.design: A red field with a white crescent and a five-pointed star.
TR.meaning: Red banners are centuries old in Turkish history. The crescent and star, already Ottoman emblems, were kept by the republic. Folklore ties them to a reflection of moon and star in a pool of blood after a battle at Kosovo — a legend, not the official origin.
TR.emblem: A crescent and star, among the world’s most copied flag charges.

TM.design: A green field with a vertical carpet-gül stripe, a white crescent, and five stars.
TM.meaning: Green is Islam and the land. The five carpet motifs are the main tribes. The crescent is hope; five stars are the regions. A wreath of olive was added after neutrality was recognized.

colors.name: Maroon
colors.meaning: The carpet stripe of the tribes

TM.emblem: Five carpet güls, a crescent, five stars, and an olive wreath of neutrality.

TC.design: A British Blue Ensign with a shield of a conch, a lobster, and a cactus.
TC.meaning: The Union Jack marks a British overseas territory. The three charges are famous local things: a queen conch, a spiny lobster, and a Turk’s cap cactus — the plant that named the islands.

colors.name: Blue
colors.meaning: The sea, on a Blue Ensign

TC.coatOfArms: The fly shield is the coat of arms, those three island emblems under a pelican.

TV.design: A light-blue British ensign with nine yellow stars in the fly.
TV.meaning: The Union Jack records links to the Commonwealth. Light blue is the Pacific. Nine stars are the nine islands, mapped roughly in their real positions.
TV.emblem: Nine stars laid out like the map of Tuvalu.

UG.design: Six stripes of black, yellow, and red with a white disc holding a grey crowned crane.
UG.meaning: Black is the people, yellow the sun, red brotherhood — the colors of the Uganda People’s Congress, adopted as national colors. The crane is a gentle bird and a former military badge.
UG.emblem: A grey crowned crane, the national bird, facing the hoist.

UA.design: Two equal horizontal bands of blue and yellow.
UA.meaning: Blue is the sky; yellow is the wheat fields — a landscape flag. The same pairing appears in medieval banners and was restored after the Soviet period.

AE.design: A vertical red band at the hoist and three horizontal bands of green, white, and black.
AE.meaning: Pan-Arab colors. Green is fertility, white neutrality and good deeds, black the oil wealth and a dark past overcome, red the union of the emirates and historic Gulf flags.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The union and historic emirate flags

GB.design: The Union Jack: the red cross of St. George, the white saltire of St. Andrew, and the red saltire of St. Patrick on blue.
GB.meaning: A stacked emblem of three kingdoms. England’s cross, Scotland’s saltire, and Ireland’s saltire (for the 1801 union) share one flag. Wales is not separately shown; it was already legally part of England.

colors.name: White
colors.meaning: St. Andrew and the fimbriation of the crosses

GB.emblem: Three patron-saint crosses combined, not a coat of arms — though the royal arms tell a related story.

US.design: Thirteen red and white stripes with a blue canton of 50 white stars.
US.meaning: Stripes are the 13 original colonies. Stars are the 50 states. Red is valor, white purity, and blue justice — a reading popularized in the 18th century. The current 50-star canton dates from Hawaii’s statehood.
US.coatOfArms: The Great Seal (eagle, shield, olive, arrows) is not on the flag; the stars and stripes do that work.

UM.design: The flag of the United States, used for the uninhabited Minor Outlying Islands.
UM.meaning: These Pacific and Caribbean islets have no separate territorial flag, so the 50-star U.S. flag stands in.

VI.design: A white field with a simplified U.S. coat of arms between the blue letters V and I.
VI.meaning: An American eagle holds an olive branch and three arrows for the three main islands. The letters name the territory. A rare flag that borrows the U.S. arms almost whole.
VI.coatOfArms: A simplified Great Seal of the United States, used as the territorial emblem.

UY.design: Nine white and blue stripes with a white canton holding the golden Sun of May.
UY.meaning: Nine stripes are the original nine departments. Blue and white come from Argentina’s revolutionary colors. The Sun of May is the same independence sun used by Argentina.
UY.emblem: The Sun of May, a face in a sunburst.

UZ.design: Three horizontal bands of blue, white, and green edged in red, with a white crescent and 12 stars in the upper hoist.
UZ.meaning: Blue is the sky and water, white peace, green nature and Islam. Thin red lines are the life force. The crescent is a young republic; 12 stars are the months and the constellations of the year.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The life force in the fimbriation

VU.design: A black hoist triangle and horizontal bands of red and green, divided by a gold Y edged in black, with a boar’s tusk and two crossed namele leaves.
VU.meaning: Red is blood and unity, green the islands, black the Melanesian people, gold the light of the gospel. The tusk is prosperity; the leaves are peace, their 39 leaflets the members of the first parliament.
VU.emblem: A boar’s tusk and namele leaves inside the gold Y.

VA.design: A vertical bicolor of gold and white with the papal tiara and crossed keys on the white band.
VA.meaning: Gold and white are the keys of St. Peter — gold for heaven, silver-white for earth. The tiara and keys are the pope’s authority. One of only two square national flags, with Switzerland.

colors.name: White
colors.meaning: The key of earth, and the papal color

VA.coatOfArms: The tiara and crossed keys on the flag are the papal arms.

VE.design: Three horizontal bands of yellow, blue, and red with an arc of eight white stars on the blue.
VE.meaning: Gran Colombia colors. Yellow is wealth, blue the sea that separates from Spain, red the blood of independence. Eight stars are the seven original provinces plus Guayana.

colors.name: Blue
colors.meaning: The sea between Venezuela and Spain

VE.emblem: Eight stars in an arc. The state flag also adds the coat of arms at the upper hoist.

VN.design: A red field with a large yellow five-pointed star.
VN.meaning: Red is the revolution and the blood of the people. The star’s five points are workers, peasants, soldiers, intellectuals, and youth — united under socialism.

colors.name: Yellow
colors.meaning: The star of the five classes, and the Vietnamese people

WF.design: A red field with a white cross and the French tricolor in the canton — a popular local flag. Officially France’s flag flies.
WF.meaning: Red and the cross come from the historic flags of Uvea (Wallis). The tricolor in the canton marks the French territory. Four triangles sometimes stand for the kings of the islands.

colors.name: White
colors.meaning: The cross of the local design

EH.design: Black, white, and green horizontal bands with a red triangle at the hoist and a red crescent and star on the white.
EH.meaning: Pan-Arab colors of the Polisario Front and the Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic. The crescent and star are Islam. Morocco’s flag is used in the areas it administers.

colors.name: Black
colors.meaning: A Pan-Arab color of the revolt

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The triangle and the Islamic star and crescent

YE.design: Three equal horizontal bands of red, white, and black.
YE.meaning: Arab Liberation colors, chosen at unification of North and South Yemen. Red is the struggle, white a bright future, black the dark past — no star or script, so both former flags could be left behind.

ZM.design: A green field with a vertical tricolor of red, black, and orange at the fly and an orange eagle above it.
ZM.meaning: Green is the land. Red is the struggle for freedom, black the people, orange mineral wealth (especially copper). The eagle is the people’s ability to rise above problems.

colors.name: Green
colors.meaning: The natural resources of the land

ZM.emblem: An African fish eagle in flight, facing the hoist — unusual for sitting in the fly rather than the center.

ZW.design: Seven stripes of green, yellow, red, and black with a white hoist triangle holding a red star and the yellow Zimbabwe Bird.
ZW.meaning: Green is the land, yellow mineral wealth, red the blood of the struggle, black the people. White is peace. The star is internationalism; the bird is a soapstone carving from Great Zimbabwe.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The blood of the liberation war

ZW.emblem: The Zimbabwe Bird on a red star, taken from medieval stone sculptures at Great Zimbabwe.

US-AL.design: A crimson saltire on a white field — a St. Andrew’s cross.
US-AL.meaning: The crimson cross recalls the Confederate battle flag’s saltire, adopted in the 1890s. There is no official color symbolism beyond that historic reference, which remains controversial.

US-AK.design: A dark-blue field with eight gold stars: the Big Dipper and Polaris.
US-AK.meaning: Blue is the sky and the forget-me-not, the state flower. The Dipper is a gold-miner’s guide and a symbol of strength; the North Star is the most northerly state. Designed by 13-year-old Benny Benson.

colors.name: Blue
colors.meaning: The evening sky and the forget-me-not

colors.name: Gold
colors.meaning: Alaska’s gold and the stars of the northern sky

US-AK.emblem: Ursa Major and Polaris, the North Star.

US-AZ.design: A copper star in front of 13 red and gold rays, over a blue lower half.
US-AZ.meaning: The copper star is the state’s great mineral. Red and gold are the colors of Spain, which once claimed the land, and also a setting sun over the desert. Blue is the same liberty blue as the U.S. flag.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The Spanish Cross of Burgundy, and a desert sunset

colors.name: Gold
colors.meaning: The Spanish colors, and the sun

US-AZ.emblem: A copper star in a sunburst of 13 rays for the 13 original colonies.

US-AR.design: A red field with a large white diamond bordered in blue, 25 white stars around the border, and four blue stars around the name Arkansas.
US-AR.meaning: The diamond is the only U.S. state with a diamond mine. Twenty-five stars mark Arkansas as the 25th state. Of the four inner stars, three are the countries that held the land (Spain, France, the U.S.) and one is the Confederacy — a remnant that is still debated.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The field, matching other historic U.S. flags

colors.name: Blue
colors.meaning: The border and the inner stars

US-AR.emblem: A diamond, 25 border stars, and four inner stars around the state name.

US-CA.design: A white field with a red stripe at the bottom, a grizzly bear, a red star, and the words California Republic.
US-CA.meaning: Copied from the 1846 Bear Flag Revolt. The bear is strength; the red star nods to the Lone Star of Texas and to independence. The republic lasted a few weeks, but the flag became the state banner.

colors.name: White
colors.meaning: The field of the Bear Flag

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The star, the stripe, and valor

US-CA.emblem: A walking grizzly bear and a single red star.
US-CA.coatOfArms: The state seal is a different, busier design. The flag uses the revolt’s bear instead.

US-CO.design: Three stripes of blue, white, and blue with a red C around a gold disc.
US-CO.meaning: Blue is the sky, white the snowcapped peaks, red the soil, and gold the sunshine. The C is Colorado. A clean, modern design that vexillologists often rank among the best state flags.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The reddish soil — colorado means “colored red”

US-CO.emblem: A red C enclosing a gold sun.

US-CT.design: A azure field with the rococo state arms: three grapevines and the motto Qui Transtulit Sustinet.
US-CT.meaning: The vines are the colony’s founding towns, transplanted from England. The Latin motto means “He who transplanted still sustains.” A classic seal-on-blue flag.

colors.name: Azure
colors.meaning: The field of the state flag

colors.name: White and gold
colors.meaning: The ornate shield and motto scroll

US-CT.coatOfArms: Three grapevines on a baroque shield — the flag is those colonial arms on blue.

US-DE.design: A colonial buff field with the coat of arms in a diamond and the date December 7, 1787.
US-DE.meaning: Buff and blue were Revolutionary War uniform colors. The date is the day Delaware became the first state to ratify the Constitution. The arms show a farmer, a soldier, an ox, wheat, and a ship.

colors.name: Buff
colors.meaning: Revolutionary uniforms, and a unique state-flag field

US-DE.coatOfArms: Agriculture and commerce supporting a shield — First State pride written as a date under the diamond.

US-FL.design: A red saltire on white with the state seal at the crossing.
US-FL.meaning: The red cross is another 19th-century St. Andrew’s design. The seal shows a Seminole woman, a sabal palm, a steamboat, and the sun — tourism-era Florida in one picture.
US-FL.coatOfArms: The Great Seal of Florida sits on the cross: palm, water, and the words “In God We Trust.”

US-GA.design: Three bars of red-white-red with a blue canton of 13 stars around the state coat of arms.
US-GA.meaning: The layout echoes the first Confederate national flag, but the current version dropped the battle-flag emblem used from 1956 to 2001. The arch and pillars are the state constitution; the motto is Wisdom, Justice, Moderation.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The bars of the historic design

US-GA.coatOfArms: The state arms in gold in the canton, ringed by 13 stars for the original colonies.

US-HI.design: Eight white-red-blue stripes with a Union Jack in the canton.
US-HI.meaning: The only U.S. state flag with the Union Jack, a leftover from the Hawaiian Kingdom’s friendship with Britain. Eight stripes are the eight main islands. It served as a national flag before annexation.

colors.name: White, red, and blue
colors.meaning: The eight islands, and the British-influenced royal palette

US-HI.emblem: The Union Jack of the Hawaiian Kingdom, kept after statehood.

US-ID.design: A blue field with the state seal and a red-scroll nameplate reading Idaho.
US-ID.meaning: A seal-on-blue flag. The seal shows a woman for justice, a miner, an elk’s head, and the motto Esto Perpetua (“Let it be perpetual”).

colors.name: Blue
colors.meaning: The field used by many U.S. state flags

US-ID.coatOfArms: The full state seal, with miner and liberty figure, centered on blue.

US-IL.design: A white field with the state seal and the name Illinois.
US-IL.meaning: The seal is an eagle landing on a rock, a shield, and a rising sun over water, with the dates 1818 and 1868. The current design added the state name so the white flag would be easier to identify.
US-IL.coatOfArms: The state seal: eagle, shield, and sun — Illinois is considering a simpler redesign.

US-IN.design: A blue field with a gold torch, 13 outer stars, five inner stars, and a larger star for Indiana.
US-IN.meaning: The torch is liberty and enlightenment. Thirteen stars are the original states; five more are the next states admitted; the large star is Indiana, the 19th state.
US-IN.emblem: A torch in a ring of stars, one of the clearer U.S. state emblems.

US-IA.design: A vertical tricolor of blue, white, and red with an eagle holding a ribbon that reads Our Liberties We Prize and Our Rights We Will Maintain.
US-IA.meaning: The French tricolor honors the Louisiana Purchase. The eagle and motto are from the state seal — a seal-on-tricolor rather than seal-on-blue.
US-IA.coatOfArms: A bald eagle and the state motto on the white band.

US-KS.design: A blue field with the state seal, a sunflower above it, and the name Kansas below.
US-KS.meaning: The sunflower is the state flower. The seal shows pioneers, a steamboat, and buffalo — “Ad Astra per Aspera” (to the stars through difficulties). The name was added so the flag would not be another anonymous blue banner.
US-KS.coatOfArms: The state seal under a sunflower.

US-KY.design: A blue field with the state seal: two men embracing, the motto United We Stand, Divided We Fall, and a goldenrod wreath.
US-KY.meaning: The handshake is friendship between frontiersman and statesman — unity of the commonwealth. Goldenrod is the state flower. Another seal-on-blue design.
US-KY.coatOfArms: The two figures and motto of the state seal, ringed in goldenrod.

US-LA.design: A blue field with a pelican feeding her young and the motto Union, Justice, Confidence.
US-LA.meaning: The “pelican in her piety” is an old Christian emblem of sacrifice — the mother bird was said to wound herself to feed her chicks. It became Louisiana’s symbol in the colonial era.
US-LA.emblem: A brown pelican tearing her breast, three drops of blood visible in the modern drawing.

US-ME.design: A blue field with the state coat of arms: a farmer, a sailor, a moose, a pine, and the motto Dirigo.
US-ME.meaning: Dirigo means “I lead,” for the North Star. The pine and moose are Maine’s woods; farmer and sailor are work on land and sea. Maine also has a simpler pine-tree merchant flag that some prefer.
US-ME.coatOfArms: The full arms on blue, with the North Star over a pine-tree shield.

US-MD.design: A quartered banner of the Calvert (black and gold) and Crossland (red and white) arms.
US-MD.meaning: Lord Baltimore’s family arms, used since colonial days. Black-and-gold paly is Calvert; the red-and-white cross bottony is his mother’s Crossland family. One of the few U.S. state flags that is a true heraldic banner.
US-MD.coatOfArms: The flag is the coat of arms, not a seal pasted on a field.

US-MA.design: A white field with the state coat of arms: an Algonquian figure holding a bow, a star, and the motto Ense petit placidam sub libertate quietem.
US-MA.meaning: The armed figure is a Massachusetts Native man, drawn as an emblem of the colony. The Latin motto means “By the sword we seek peace, but peace only under liberty.” A gold pine tree on the reverse was dropped; a redesign is under discussion.
US-MA.coatOfArms: The full arms on white, including a disembodied sword arm over the shield.

US-MI.design: A blue field with the state coat of arms: an elk and a moose, an eagle, a man at a lake, and the mottos Tuebor and Si Quaeris Peninsulam Amoenam Circumspice.
US-MI.meaning: Tuebor means “I will defend.” The longer motto means “If you seek a pleasant peninsula, look about you.” The waters are the Great Lakes. A busy seal-on-blue flag.
US-MI.coatOfArms: The full arms, with elk, moose, and eagle supporters.

US-MN.design: A light-blue fly with a dark-blue hoist shape of the state, charged with a white eight-pointed North Star.
US-MN.meaning: The new flag dropped a seal that showed a settler and a Native rider. Light blue is the Land of 10,000 Lakes. The dark shape is Minnesota itself. The star is L’Étoile du Nord, the state motto.

colors.name: Dark blue
colors.meaning: The shape of the state, and night sky

US-MN.emblem: An eight-pointed North Star on the silhouette of Minnesota.
US-MN.coatOfArms: The 2024 seal (a loon and wild rice) is no longer on the flag; the star replaced it.

US-MS.design: A vertical tricolor of blue, gold, and red with a white magnolia in a gold-star circle and the words In God We Trust.
US-MS.meaning: Replaced a flag that included the Confederate battle emblem. The magnolia is hospitality and the state flower. Twenty stars are the 20th state; a gold starburst honors indigenous peoples.

colors.name: Gold
colors.meaning: The bars and the honor star

US-MS.emblem: A magnolia blossom in a ring of stars — the “New Magnolia” flag.

US-MO.design: A horizontal tricolor of red, white, and blue with the state seal in the center.
US-MO.meaning: The U.S. colors. The seal has two grizzlies, a crescent for a second-born son (Missouri was the second state carved from the Purchase), and the motto Salus Populi Suprema Lex Esto.
US-MO.coatOfArms: The full seal in a blue ring of 24 stars, for the 24th state.

US-MT.design: A blue field with the state seal and the name Montana in gold.
US-MT.meaning: The seal shows mountains, the Great Falls of the Missouri, a plow, and a pick — “gold and silver” in the motto Oro y Plata. The name was added in 1981.

colors.name: Gold
colors.meaning: The state name, and the motto’s gold

US-MT.coatOfArms: The territorial-era seal, still used as the state seal.

US-NE.design: A blue field with the state seal in gold and silver.
US-NE.meaning: A seal-on-blue flag. The seal shows a steamboat, a train, a cabin, and a smith — settlement of the plains — with the motto Equality Before the Law.
US-NE.coatOfArms: The state seal, adopted in 1867, placed on blue in the 1960s.

US-NV.design: A blue field with a wreath of sagebrush, a silver star, and the words Battle Born in the canton.
US-NV.meaning: Battle Born marks statehood during the Civil War. The star is silver, the state metal. Sagebrush is the state plant. A much cleaner canton than the old seal-on-blue version.
US-NV.emblem: A silver star in sagebrush with the Battle Born scroll.

US-NH.design: A blue field with the state seal: the frigate Raleigh under construction.
US-NH.meaning: The Raleigh was a Revolutionary War warship built at Portsmouth. The seal celebrates that shipyard moment. Another seal-on-blue flag.
US-NH.coatOfArms: The 1784 seal, redrawn to show the Raleigh more clearly, on blue.

US-NJ.design: A buff field with the state coat of arms: Liberty and Ceres, a horse’s head, and three plows.
US-NJ.meaning: Buff and blue were Washington’s New Jersey livery colors. Liberty and Ceres (agriculture) support a shield of plows. The motto is Liberty and Prosperity.

colors.name: Buff
colors.meaning: Washington’s New Jersey uniforms, shared with Delaware

US-NJ.coatOfArms: The full arms on buff — one of the few non-blue state fields.

US-NM.design: A gold field with a red Zia sun: a circle and four groups of four rays.
US-NM.meaning: Red and gold are the colors of Spain. The Zia sun is a Pueblo sacred emblem: four is the number of the directions, the seasons, the ages of life, and the day’s times. Widely ranked the best U.S. state flag.
US-NM.emblem: The Zia sun symbol, used with the pueblo’s permission and still treated as sacred.

US-NY.design: A blue field with the state coat of arms: Liberty and Justice, a Hudson scene, and the motto Excelsior.
US-NY.meaning: Excelsior means “ever upward.” The shield is the Hudson River with a sun and mountains. Liberty’s crown is at her feet, for independence from Britain.
US-NY.coatOfArms: The full arms, including an eagle on a globe above the shield.

US-NC.design: A blue hoist with a white star and the dates May 20, 1775 and April 12, 1776, plus a red-over-white fly.
US-NC.meaning: The dates are the Mecklenburg Declaration and the Halifax Resolves, early independence claims. The star is liberty. The red-white fly recalls North Carolina’s role in the Revolution.

colors.name: White
colors.meaning: The star and the lower fly

US-NC.emblem: A single star between two historic dates.

US-ND.design: A blue field with a modified U.S. coat of arms, a scroll reading North Dakota, and a ring of stars.
US-ND.meaning: An eagle-and-shield design close to the national arms, used by the state militia before it became the state flag. The name banner identifies it.
US-ND.coatOfArms: A unit banner that became a state flag, still looking like a military color.

US-OH.design: A swallowtail burgee: blue triangle with 17 stars and a white-and-red O, plus red and white stripes.
US-OH.meaning: The only non-rectangular U.S. state flag. Seventeen stars mark Ohio as the 17th state. The O is Ohio and a buckeye. Stripes nod to the U.S. flag. Designed by John Eisenmann for the 1901 Pan-American Exposition.

colors.name: Red, white, and blue
colors.meaning: The United States, in a burgee shape

US-OH.emblem: A red disc with a white ring — the O and the buckeye.

US-OK.design: A sky-blue field with an Osage war shield, seven eagle feathers, and a calumet crossed with an olive branch.
US-OK.meaning: Sky blue is a common Native flag color of the southern plains. The shield is defense; the pipe and olive branch are peace. Designed by Choctaw student Louise Fluke in 1925; the name word was later removed to clean the design.

colors.name: Sky blue
colors.meaning: Peace, and a traditional plains flag color

US-OK.emblem: An Osage shield with pipe and olive — peace over war.

US-OR.design: A navy field with the state seal in gold on the front and a gold beaver on the back — the only two-sided U.S. state flag.
US-OR.meaning: The seal shows mountains, a wagon, a ship, and a sheaf — the Oregon Trail in heraldry. The beaver is the state animal and a fur-trade emblem.
US-OR.coatOfArms: The state seal on the obverse; a beaver on the reverse.

US-PA.design: A blue field with the state coat of arms: two horses, a shield of a ship, a plow, and three sheaves, and the motto Virtue, Liberty and Independence.
US-PA.meaning: Commerce, farming, and plenty on the shield. The horses are draft animals of the commonwealth. A typical seal-on-blue Revolutionary-era design.
US-PA.coatOfArms: The full arms, including an eagle crest, on blue.

US-RI.design: A white field with a gold anchor, 13 gold stars, and the motto Hope.
US-RI.meaning: The anchor and Hope come from the colony’s 1640s seal, a biblical emblem for a refuge. Thirteen stars are the original states. A clean, old design that ranks well among state flags.
US-RI.emblem: An anchor and the word Hope, Rhode Island’s oldest symbol.

US-SC.design: A blue field with a white palmetto tree and a white crescent in the canton.
US-SC.meaning: The crescent is from Revolutionary War caps. The palmetto recalls the palmetto-log fort that stopped British cannon at Sullivan’s Island in 1776. A simple, beloved design.
US-SC.emblem: A palmetto and a crescent, both from the Revolution.

US-SD.design: A sky-blue field with the state seal in a sunburst and the words South Dakota and The Mount Rushmore State.
US-SD.meaning: A seal-in-sun design. The seal shows farming, mining, and a riverboat. The nickname replaced “The Sunshine State,” which Florida also claimed.
US-SD.coatOfArms: The state seal inside a serrated gold sun.

US-TN.design: A red field with a blue stripe at the fly, a white-edged blue disc, and three white stars.
US-TN.meaning: The three stars are East, Middle, and West Tennessee, bound in one circle. Blue is the river-bound unity of the grand divisions. A distinctive, well-liked design by Colonel LeRoy Reeves.

colors.name: Blue
colors.meaning: The disc and the fly bar

colors.name: White
colors.meaning: The three stars and the fimbriation

US-TN.emblem: Three stars in a circle for the three Grand Divisions.

US-TX.design: A blue vertical hoist with a single white star, and two horizontal bands of white and red.
US-TX.meaning: The Lone Star is the Republic of Texas, an independent country before it joined the Union. Blue is loyalty, white purity, red bravery — the same readings as the U.S. flag. One of two state flags that were national flags (with Hawaii).

US-UT.design: A dark-blue field with a white hexagon, a gold beehive, a white star, and red-and-white mountain stripes at the fly.
US-UT.meaning: The 2024 beehive flag replaced a seal-on-blue design. Blue is the sky and faith; white the peaks and peace; red the red-rock canyons and perseverance. The hive is industry; the star is the 45th state.
US-UT.emblem: A beehive in a hexagon with a star — unity, industry, and statehood.
US-UT.coatOfArms: The old seal with sego lilies is no longer on the flag; the hive now carries that story.

US-VT.design: A blue field with the state coat of arms: a pine, a cow, sheaves, and the motto Freedom and Unity.
US-VT.meaning: The pine and cow are rural Vermont. Freedom and Unity is the state motto. An earlier 16-star, 17-stripe flag was dropped because it looked too much like the U.S. flag.
US-VT.coatOfArms: The full arms on blue, with a deer crest above the pine-tree shield.

US-VA.design: A blue field with the state seal: Virtus standing over a fallen tyrant, and the motto Sic Semper Tyrannis.
US-VA.meaning: Virtus is virtue dressed as a Amazon; the fallen king is tyranny. The motto means “Thus always to tyrants.” Adopted as a secession-era banner and kept.
US-VA.coatOfArms: The 1776 seal, one of the most dramatic state emblems, placed on blue.

US-WA.design: A dark-green field with the state seal: a portrait of George Washington and the date 1889.
US-WA.meaning: Green is the Evergreen State. The seal is the first president’s face — the only U.S. state flag with a president’s portrait. 1889 is the year of statehood.
US-WA.coatOfArms: Gilbert Stuart’s Washington, ringed in gold, on green.

US-WV.design: A white field bordered in blue with the state coat of arms: a farmer, a miner, a rock dated June 20, 1863, and the motto Montani Semper Liberi.
US-WV.meaning: June 20, 1863 is statehood day, when West Virginia split from Virginia during the Civil War. The motto means “Mountaineers are always free.”
US-WV.coatOfArms: The farmer-and-miner arms with a Phrygian cap and rifles, on white.

US-WI.design: A blue field with the state coat of arms and the name Wisconsin above the date 1848.
US-WI.meaning: The arms show a sailor and a miner, a badger crest, and the motto Forward. 1848 is statehood. The name and date were added so the flag would not vanish among other blue seals.
US-WI.coatOfArms: The full arms, including a badger, on blue.

US-WY.design: A blue field with a red-and-white border and a white bison charged with the state seal.
US-WY.meaning: The bison is the state mammal. The seal on its side shows a woman, a miner, and a cowboy. Red is the Native peoples and the blood of pioneers; white is purity; blue is the sky and fidelity.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The border, for Native peoples and pioneers

US-WY.emblem: A bison silhouette with the state seal on its shoulder — a seal-on-animal rather than seal-on-blue.
